lessons.title: Math is Mine
lessons.objective: I can describe the ways we are all doers of math, and compare my math story with a classmate's.
lessons.languageObjective: I can tell my math story using the words strength, challenge, and I use math when ___ .

vocabulary.definition: Anyone who uses mathematical thinking — which is everyone, every day.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquiera que use el pensamiento matemático, es decir, todos, todos los días.

vocabulary.definition: Your own history with mathematics — what you have done, felt, and learned so far.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tu propia historia con las matemáticas: lo que has hecho, sentido y aprendido.

vocabulary.definition: Something you already do well and can share with others.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que ya haces bien y puedes compartir con otros.

vocabulary.definition: To break a number into parts that add, subtract, multiply, or divide back to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un número en partes que se combinan para volver a formarlo.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, without counting every one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin contar todo.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The Ferris wheel has 20 cars, and about 4 people fit in each car. About how many people can ride at one time?
I count the cars: 20. Then I estimate how many riders fit in one car: about 4.
I do not count every person — an estimate is a reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful.
20 × 4 = 80, so I would say “about 80 people.”
instructional.commonMistake: Believing that 'doing math' only counts when it happens on paper in a classroom.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Everyone uses math every day — at home, at school, and in the neighborhood. When a problem feels big, first understand it, then break it into smaller parts and keep trying. A quick estimate or mental math helps you check if your answer makes sense.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Todos usamos las matemáticas todos los días: en casa, en la escuela y en el vecindario. Cuando un problema parece grande, primero hay que entenderlo, luego dividirlo en partes más pequeñas y seguir intentando. Una estimación rápida o el cálculo mental ayudan a comprobar si la respuesta tiene sentido.

lessons.title: Math is Exploring and Thinking
lessons.objective: I can make sense of a problem, plan a strategy, and use fractions of a whole number to compare quantities.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my plan using the words we know, we don't know, and my strategy is ___ .

vocabulary.definition: An amount in a problem — a number with a meaning attached, like 540 meters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad en un problema: un número con un significado, como 540 metros.

vocabulary.definition: How two quantities compare or connect to each other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se comparan o se conectan dos cantidades entre sí.

vocabulary.definition: A plan for how to solve a problem before you start computing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un plan para resolver un problema antes de empezar a calcular.

vocabulary.definition: A solution that makes sense in the context of the problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una solución que tiene sentido en el contexto del problema.

vocabulary.definition: To keep working on a problem, checking your progress and adjusting your plan when you get stuck.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Seguir trabajando en un problema, revisando tu progreso y ajustando tu plan cuando te atascas.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A bowl is full of peas — far too many to count one at a time. About how many peas are in the bowl?
I do not count every pea — I look for a group I CAN count, like one small cluster of about 10.
Then I ask how many of those clusters would cover the whole bowl. I count about 12.
12 clusters of about 10 is 12 × 10 = 120, so my estimate is about 120 peas — a reasoned answer, close enough to be useful.
instructional.commonMistake: Expecting a fraction of a number to be bigger than the number — 5/6 × 540 must be LESS than 540 because 5/6 is less than 1; only a fraction greater than 1, like 6/5, makes the product bigger.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Before solving, find what you already know and what the question is asking. Pick a plan, like drawing a picture, writing an equation, or making a table. Check how it is going, and try a new plan if you get stuck.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Antes de resolver, hay que identificar lo que ya se sabe y lo que pregunta el problema. Luego se elige un plan, como hacer un dibujo, escribir una ecuación o hacer una tabla. Hay que revisar cómo va el trabajo y probar otro plan si uno se atora.

lessons.title: Math is In My World
lessons.objective: I can represent a real-world situation with a tape diagram or table and use decimal operations to solve it.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe my tool using the words tape diagram, table, and this represents ___ .

vocabulary.definition: A picture, diagram, table, or equation that shows the mathematics in a situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un dibujo, diagrama, tabla o ecuación que muestra las matemáticas de una situación.

vocabulary.definition: A rectangle cut into equal parts that helps you visualize how a total breaks apart.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un rectángulo dividido en partes iguales que te ayuda a visualizar cómo se separa un total.

vocabulary.definition: Anything you choose to help you see relationships and solve a problem — a table, a diagram, a graph.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier cosa que eliges para ver relaciones y resolver un problema: una tabla, un diagrama, una gráfica.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers that go together, like a time and a number of trips, that you can plot as a point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números que van juntos, como un tiempo y un número de viajes, que puedes graficar como un punto.

vocabulary.definition: A complete journey from the start, to the destination, and back to the start.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un recorrido completo desde el inicio hasta el destino y de regreso al inicio.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A pile of coins is too big to count one at a time. About how many coins are in the pile?
I do not count every coin — I find a small stack I CAN count, about 10 coins.
Then I estimate how many stacks like that are in the pile. I count about 15.
15 stacks of about 10 is 15 × 10 = 150, so my estimate is about 150 coins — reasoned, not random.
instructional.commonMistake: Converting minutes to hours by moving the decimal point — 625 minutes is NOT 6.25 hours. An hour is 60 minutes, so divide by 60: 625 ÷ 60 ≈ 10.42 hours.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Pick a tool that helps you see the math, like a tape diagram (a bar split into equal parts), a number line, or a grid. Label every part and its units. Then use the picture to write the number sentence that matches it.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Hay que elegir una herramienta que ayude a ver las matemáticas, como un diagrama de cintas (una barra dividida en partes iguales), una recta numérica o una cuadrícula. Se rotula cada parte con sus unidades. Luego se usa el dibujo para escribir la operación que le corresponde.

lessons.title: Math is Explaining and Sharing
lessons.objective: I can construct an argument using equations, drawings, or words, and use volume to defend a recommendation.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my thinking with clear math vocabulary using the words argument, conjecture, and cubic units.

vocabulary.definition: A chain of reasons — equations, drawings, or words — used to defend your thinking.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cadena de razones — ecuaciones, dibujos o palabras — que usas para defender tu pensamiento.

vocabulary.definition: A mathematical statement you believe is true but have not yet proven.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una afirmación matemática que crees verdadera pero que aún no has probado.

vocabulary.definition: A single example that shows a statement is not always true.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo ejemplo que muestra que una afirmación no siempre es verdadera.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of space a solid figure takes up, measured in cubic units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio que ocupa una figura sólida, medida en unidades cúbicas.

vocabulary.definition: A cube with edges 1 unit long — the unit used to measure volume.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un cubo cuyas aristas miden 1 unidad — la unidad que se usa para medir el volumen.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Suppose each large box is 8 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. Its volume is 8 × 3 × 10 = 240 cubic inches, so three large boxes hold 240 × 3 = 720 cubic inches.
Suppose each jumbo box is 10 inches long, 4 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. Its volume is 10 × 4 × 10 = 400 cubic inches, so two jumbo boxes hold 400 × 2 = 800 cubic inches.
I recommend buying two jumbo boxes because 800 cubic inches is greater than 720 cubic inches — the total volume is greater, so there is more cereal for the same price.
instructional.commonMistake: Reporting volume without cubic units — saying the garden needs '48 feet' of soil, which is a length, or '48 square feet', which is an area.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Make a clear claim and back it up with math. Use the right units and words, like cubic units for volume. Then test your idea with more examples, and look for one example that would show it is not always true.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Hay que hacer una afirmación clara y respaldarla con cálculos. Se usan las unidades y palabras correctas, como unidades cúbicas para el volumen. Luego se pone a prueba la idea con más ejemplos y se busca un ejemplo que muestre que no siempre es verdad.

lessons.title: Math is Finding Patterns
lessons.objective: I can find patterns and pattern rules, use them to make generalizations, and check my solutions with a table of values.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe a pattern using the words pattern rule, generalization, and 'each number is ___ more than the one before it.'

vocabulary.definition: Something that repeats or changes in a predictable way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que se repite o cambia de una manera predecible.

vocabulary.definition: The instruction that tells how to get from one number in a pattern to the next.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La instrucción que dice cómo pasar de un número del patrón al siguiente.

vocabulary.definition: A statement that is true for a whole pattern, made by noticing repeated calculations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una afirmación verdadera para todo un patrón, hecha al notar cálculos repetidos.

vocabulary.definition: A table that lists each step of a pattern so you can check that a solution is reasonable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla que muestra cada paso de un patrón para comprobar que una solución es razonable.

vocabulary.definition: Whether an answer makes sense — checked as you work, with adjustments made when needed.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Si una respuesta tiene sentido — se comprueba mientras trabajas y se ajusta cuando es necesario.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A change jar is full of pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters worth $53.50 in total. How many of each coin could there be?
Each penny has a value of $0.01, so 100 pennies have a value of $1.00.

Each nickel has a value of $0.05, so 100 nickels have a value of $5.00. Each dime has a value of $0.10, so 100 dimes have a value of $10. Each quarter has a value of $0.25, so 100 quarters have a value of $25.
I multiply the number of each coin by its value. And I notice a generalization: because the jar's total, $53.50, ends in 0, the number of pennies can only be a multiple of 5.
instructional.commonMistake: Reporting only the points from the streak (20 or 30) and forgetting to add the points each player had before the streak began.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Write what you notice in a table. Look for the rule that stays the same from one step to the next. Then write that rule so you can predict what comes next.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Se anota en una tabla lo que se observa. Se busca la regla que se mantiene igual de un paso al siguiente. Luego se escribe esa regla para poder predecir lo que sigue.

lessons.title: Math is Ours
lessons.objective: I can describe my problem-solving process, name strategies for getting unstuck, and identify the behaviors that make our class a community of math thinkers.
lessons.languageObjective: I can talk about problem solving using the phrases make sense of, get stuck, try a strategy, and work together.

vocabulary.definition: To figure out what a problem is asking — what you know, and what you don't know yet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Descubrir qué pide un problema: qué sabes y qué no sabes todavía.

vocabulary.definition: A way of showing a problem — a drawing, table, equation, or model — that helps you see it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma de mostrar un problema — un dibujo, una tabla, una ecuación o un modelo — que te ayuda a verlo.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of attack for a problem — and something you can switch when you get stuck.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un plan para atacar un problema — y algo que puedes cambiar cuando te atascas.

vocabulary.definition: To examine an idea and say what is convincing or not — about the idea, never about the person.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Examinar una idea y decir qué es convincente o no — sobre la idea, nunca sobre la persona.

vocabulary.definition: A rule the whole class agrees to so that everyone can learn together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una norma que toda la clase acepta para que todos puedan aprender juntos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: First I make sense of it: one rack holds 8 bikes, each bike has 2 wheels, so this rack has 8 × 2 = 16 wheels. The other rack has 6 times as many wheels — that is what I don't know yet.
I choose a representation: 6 equal groups of 16. Then I make a plan: multiply.
16 × 6 = 96, so the other rack has about 96 wheels. I check my progress: 96 is 6 groups of 16, and 16 × 6 = 96, so my answer matches my plan.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's build a get-unstuck list together
instructional.commonMistake: Treating 'stuck' as a stop sign instead of a signal — waiting silently instead of trying a strategy: asking a question, drawing the problem, or recalling a similar problem.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Explain your thinking using clear math words. Listen to how your partner solved the problem and compare it with your way. Use the class agreements to work toward an answer the whole group agrees on.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Se explica el razonamiento con palabras matemáticas claras. Se escucha cómo resolvió el problema el compañero y se compara con la forma propia. Se usan los acuerdos de la clase para llegar a una respuesta en la que todo el grupo esté de acuerdo.

lessons.title: Understand Statistical Questions
lessons.objective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words statistical question, data, variability, and survey.

vocabulary.definition: A statistical question expects varied answers that can be collected as data.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta estadística espera respuestas variadas que se pueden recopilar como datos.

vocabulary.definition: A question answered with data that are expected to vary.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta que se responde con datos que se espera que varíen.

vocabulary.definition: A question that does not anticipate variability in the data used to answer it. It may ask for one fact or measurement.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta que no anticipa variabilidad en los datos usados para responderla. Puede pedir un solo dato o una medición.

vocabulary.definition: Facts and numbers you collect, like answers to a survey.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Datos y números que recoges, como respuestas a una encuesta.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: Collecting facts by asking people questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Recoger datos haciendo preguntas a las personas.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.

vocabulary.definition: A number line with one dot for each data value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una recta numérica con un punto por cada valor de los datos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Question 1: "How many points did our top player score last night?" There is one player and one game, so there is one fixed answer, like 18 points.
One answer, no variety, so this is NOT a statistical question.
Question 2: "How many points does each player score per game?" The answers vary: 8, 12, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22.
Because the answers are different for different players, I must collect data. This IS a statistical question.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Statistical Questions and Data is judging a question by its topic or its numbers instead of its variability. Students see a question about ONE player, ONE game, or ONE fixed fact — like "How many points does the team need to win a game?" — and call it statistical just because it has a number or is about sports. Or they see a question about a single player's whole season, like "How many touchdowns did the quarterback throw this season?", and call it NOT statistical because only one player is named, forgetting that a season covers many games with a different result each time. Both errors skip the real test: will the answers actually differ from case to case (game to game, player to player)? If yes, it is a statistical question; if there is one fixed answer, it is not.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A statistical question has answers that change from person to person, so you collect data to answer it. A question with only one fixed answer is not a statistical question. For example, "How tall is each student in the class?" is statistical, but "How many days are in a week?" is not.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una pregunta estadística tiene respuestas que cambian de una persona a otra, así que reúnes datos para responderla. Una pregunta con una sola respuesta fija no es estadística. Por ejemplo, «¿Cuánto mide cada estudiante de la clase?» es estadística, pero «¿Cuántos días tiene una semana?» no lo es.

lessons.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Histogram
lessons.objective: I can make and read a histogram to display data in intervals.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my histogram using the words histogram, frequency, interval, and distribution.

vocabulary.definition: Group numerical data into intervals and show each interval's frequency with a bar.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Agrupar datos numéricos en intervalos y mostrar la frecuencia de cada intervalo con una barra.

vocabulary.definition: A bar graph that groups data into equal ranges. The bars touch.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una gráfica de barras que agrupa datos en rangos iguales. Las barras se tocan.

vocabulary.definition: How many times a value shows up.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuántas veces aparece un valor.

vocabulary.definition: A range of numbers used to group data.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un rango de números para agrupar datos.

vocabulary.definition: How the data is spread out.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo están repartidos los datos.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: A table that lists each interval and how many values fall in it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla que muestra cada intervalo y cuántos valores caen en él.

vocabulary.definition: The pattern the bars or dots make across the intervals.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El patrón que forman las barras o los puntos a lo largo de los intervalos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My data: 3, 7, 12, 15, 18, 24. I will use intervals of 10: 0–9, 10–19, 20–29.
Interval 0–9: the values 3 and 7 fit, so the frequency is 2.
Interval 10–19: the values 12, 15, and 18 fit, so the frequency is 3.
Interval 20–29: only the value 24 fits, so the frequency is 1.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Display Data: Histograms is counting a boundary value in two intervals at once — for example, putting the value 10 in both the '0–9' bin and the '10–19' bin. Each data value belongs to exactly ONE interval. Before you submit, add up all your frequencies and check that the total matches the number of data values you started with.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A histogram is a bar graph that puts numbers into equal groups, like 0–9, 10–19, and 20–29. The height of each bar shows how many numbers are in that group. The bars touch, with no gaps between them.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un histograma es una gráfica de barras que pone los números en grupos iguales, como 0–9, 10–19 y 20–29. La altura de cada barra muestra cuántos números hay en ese grupo. Las barras se tocan, sin espacios entre ellas.

lessons.title: Describe the Data Using the Median
lessons.objective: I can find the median of a data set and use it to describe what is typical.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain the median using the words order, middle, typical, and half.

vocabulary.term: Describe the Data Using the Median
vocabulary.definition: Using the middle value of the ordered data to say what is typical for the whole set.
vocabulary.termEs: Describir los datos con la mediana
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar el valor del medio de los datos ordenados para decir qué es típico en todo el conjunto.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.

vocabulary.definition: The number that shows up most often.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que aparece más veces.

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: One number that describes a typical value in a data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que describe un valor típico de un conjunto de datos.

vocabulary.definition: The number exactly between the two middle values of an even-count data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que está exactamente entre los dos valores centrales de un conjunto con una cantidad par de datos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9 — five values, already in order. Ordering first is what makes a middle exist at all.
With 5 values, the middle is the 3rd one. Counting in from both ends: 2 and 9 pair off, 4 and 6 pair off, and 4 is left alone.
So the median is 4. Half the values sit at or below it and half at or above it.
Now an even set: 2, 4, 6, 9. There is no single middle, so I take the mean of the two middle values: (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5. The median is 5, even though 5 is not in the data.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Mean, Median, and Mode is finding the median without ordering the data first — students pick the middle number straight from the list as given (for 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 they say the median is 7, the middle position in that original order) instead of sorting least to greatest (2, 4, 6, 7, 9) and finding the true middle value, 6. Before finalizing a median, always reorder the data smallest to largest, then count to the middle position — and if there is an even number of values, average the two middle numbers.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: The median is the middle number after you put the numbers in order from least to greatest. If there are two middle numbers, the median is the number exactly halfway between them.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: La mediana es el número del medio después de ordenar los números de menor a mayor. Si hay dos números en el medio, la mediana es el número que está exactamente a la mitad entre ellos.

lessons.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot
lessons.objective: I can make and read a box plot to summarize a data set.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my box plot using the words box plot, median, quartile, and interquartile range.

vocabulary.definition: Show a data set's five-number summary in a box-and-whisker display.
vocabulary.termEs: Representar datos con diagramas de caja
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar el resumen de cinco números de un conjunto de datos en un diagrama de caja y bigotes.

vocabulary.definition: A graph that shows how data is spread using five key numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una gráfica que muestra cómo se reparten los datos con cinco números clave.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers that split the data into four equal parts.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números que dividen los datos en cuatro partes iguales.

vocabulary.definition: The spread of the middle half of the data (Q3 − Q1).
vocabulary.definitionEs: La extensión de la mitad central de los datos (Q3 − Q1).

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: The minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum of a data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mínimo, el primer cuartil, la mediana, el tercer cuartil y el máximo de un conjunto de datos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My data, in order: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22, 24, 28. There are 11 numbers.
The middle number is the 6th one, 14, so the median = 14.
The lower half is 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Its middle is 8, so Q1 = 8.
The upper half is 15, 18, 22, 24, 28. Its middle is 22, so Q3 = 22.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Display Data: Box Plots is treating a quartile as just one data point instead of the median of a half — for the lower half 4, 8, 10, 14, some students pick 10 (the last value) as Q1 instead of finding the median of that half: Q1 = (8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9. A second common slip is finding IQR by adding the quartiles instead of subtracting, writing IQR = Q3 + Q1 (like 30 + 18 = 48) instead of IQR = Q3 − Q1 (30 − 18 = 12) — always order the data first, then subtract Q1 from Q3 to find the spread of the middle 50%.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A box plot shows how data is spread out using five numbers: the lowest, the first quartile (Q1), the median, the third quartile (Q3), and the highest. The box goes from Q1 to Q3 and holds the middle half of the data; its length is Q3 − Q1. Lines called whiskers reach from the box out to the lowest and highest numbers.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra cómo se reparten los datos usando cinco números: el menor, el primer cuartil (Q1), la mediana, el tercer cuartil (Q3) y el mayor. La caja va de Q1 a Q3 y contiene la mitad central de los datos; su largo es Q3 − Q1. Unas líneas llamadas bigotes van desde la caja hasta el número menor y el número mayor.

lessons.title: Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range
lessons.objective: I can find the range and the interquartile range of a data set and use them to describe how spread out the data is.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain what the spread of a data set is using the words range, quartile, interquartile range, and vary.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers that describe spread: the range covers all the data, and the interquartile range covers only the middle half.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números que describen la dispersión: el rango cubre todos los datos y el rango intercuartílico solo la mitad central.

vocabulary.definition: The distance from the least value to the greatest value, found by subtracting: greatest − least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia del valor menor al mayor, que se halla restando: mayor − menor.

vocabulary.definition: One of the three values that cut an ordered data set into four equal-sized groups.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los tres valores que dividen un conjunto ordenado de datos en cuatro grupos del mismo tamaño.

vocabulary.definition: The distance across the middle half of the data, found by subtracting the first quartile from the third: Q3 − Q1.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia a lo largo de la mitad central de los datos: se resta el primer cuartil del tercero: Q3 − Q1.

vocabulary.definition: How much the values in a data set differ from one another — whether they sit close together or far apart.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto se diferencian entre sí los valores de un conjunto de datos: si están juntos o muy separados.

vocabulary.definition: A single number that describes the spread of a whole data set. The range and the IQR are both measures of variation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que describe la dispersión de todo un conjunto de datos. El rango y el RIC son medidas de variación.

vocabulary.definition: The least or greatest value in a data set, far from the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor menor o mayor de un conjunto de datos, lejos del resto.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Here are 20 history test scores in order: 68, 70, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 80, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 86, 88, 88, 90, 90, 93, 94. Ordering them first is what makes every step after this possible.
Range: I subtract the least value from the greatest. 94 − 68 = 26. The scores span 26 points from end to end.
Now the quartiles. The median splits the 20 scores into two halves of 10. The median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values: (83 + 84) ÷ 2 = 83.5.
Q1 is the median of the lower 10 values: halfway between 75 and 76, so Q1 = 75.5. Q3 is the median of the upper 10: halfway between 88 and 88, so Q3 = 88.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake with Range and Interquartile Range is adding the two quartiles instead of subtracting them — writing IQR = Q3 + Q1. With Q1 = 42 and Q3 = 58 that gives 100, which is larger than the data set's entire range of 20. Every measure of variation is a DIFFERENCE, and the IQR can never exceed the range, because the middle half is part of the whole span. If your IQR comes out bigger than your range, you added when you should have subtracted.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: The range tells how spread out all of the data is: range = greatest number − least number. The interquartile range (IQR) tells how spread out the middle half of the data is: IQR = Q3 − Q1.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El rango dice qué tan separados están todos los datos: rango = número mayor − número menor. El rango intercuartílico dice qué tan separada está la mitad central de los datos: rango intercuartílico = Q3 − Q1.

lessons.title: Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm
lessons.objective: I can divide multi-digit whole numbers and explain the meaning of the quotient and remainder.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my division using the words dividend, divisor, quotient, and remainder.

vocabulary.definition: A step-by-step set of rules or instructions to solve a math problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de pasos o instrucciones para resolver un problema de matemáticas.

vocabulary.definition: The total number being divided into equal groups (the number inside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número total que se divide en grupos iguales (el número dentro de la galera de división).

vocabulary.definition: The number of equal groups you are dividing into (the number outside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número de grupos iguales en que divides (el número fuera de la galera de división).

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.

vocabulary.definition: What is left over when a number does not divide evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que sobra cuando un número no se divide de forma exacta.

vocabulary.definition: Separate a multi-digit number into equal groups to find a quotient.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un número de varias cifras en grupos iguales para hallar un cociente.

vocabulary.definition: A method that repeats four steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until there are no digits left to bring down.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un método que repite cuatro pasos — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — hasta que no quedan dígitos por bajar.

vocabulary.definition: The fourth step of long division: move the next digit of the dividend down next to what is left, then start the cycle again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El cuarto paso de la división larga: baja el siguiente dígito del dividendo junto a lo que sobró y vuelve a empezar el ciclo.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I want 1,344 ÷ 12. The dividend is 1,344 and the divisor is 12, so 12 goes outside the bracket and 1,344 goes inside.
DIVIDE: 12 does not fit into 1, so I look at 13. How many 12s fit into 13? One. I write 1 above the 3.
MULTIPLY: 1 × 12 = 12. I write 12 underneath the 13.
SUBTRACT: 13 − 12 = 1. That is what is left so far.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Multi-Digit Numbers is skipping a placeholder zero in the quotient when a digit doesn't divide evenly, which shifts every digit after it out of place. For example, dividing 3,216 ÷ 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, but the next digit 2 doesn't divide by 3, so a 0 must be written before continuing — bring down the 1 to make 21 ÷ 3 = 7, then bring down 6 ÷ 3 = 2, giving the correct quotient 1,072. A student who skips writing that 0 and jumps straight to 21 ÷ 3 = 7 ends up with 172 instead of 1,072 — an answer off by a factor of ten. Always check: does a digit in your quotient go missing every time you 'can't divide'? If so, you dropped a placeholder zero.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Long division splits a number into equal groups, one digit at a time. Repeat four steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until there are no digits left. Anything left over at the end is the remainder.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: La división larga reparte un número en grupos iguales, un dígito a la vez. Repite cuatro pasos — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — hasta que no queden dígitos. Lo que sobre al final es el residuo.

lessons.title: Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm
lessons.objective: I can divide with decimals by making the divisor a whole number first.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words dividend, divisor, quotient, and equivalent division.

vocabulary.definition: Find a quotient with decimals by sliding both decimal points right until the divisor is a whole number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar un cociente con decimales deslizando ambos puntos decimales a la derecha hasta que el divisor sea un número entero.

vocabulary.definition: The total number being divided into equal groups (the number inside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número total que se divide en grupos iguales (el número dentro de la galera de división).

vocabulary.definition: The number of equal groups you are dividing into (the number outside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número de grupos iguales en que divides (el número fuera de la galera de división).

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.

vocabulary.definition: The steps for dividing decimals: slide the divisor's decimal point right until the divisor is a whole number, slide the dividend's point right the same number of places, then divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los pasos para dividir decimales: desliza el punto decimal del divisor a la derecha hasta que sea un número entero, desliza el punto del dividendo a la derecha el mismo número de lugares y luego divide.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying both numbers by 10 or 100 gives the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar ambos números por 10 o 100 da la misma respuesta.

vocabulary.definition: Write a zero after the last decimal digit without changing the value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un cero después del último dígito decimal sin cambiar el valor.

vocabulary.definition: A set of steps you follow the same way every time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de pasos que sigues de la misma manera cada vez.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and long division needs a whole-number divisor.
STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor, so 6.3 becomes 63.
I slide the decimal point 1 place to the right in the dividend too, so 18.9 becomes 189. Both points slid the same 1 place, so the answer does not change. The problem is now 189 ÷ 63.

Now I write it the tall way — 63 into 189 — with the answer going on top of the bar and the answer's decimal point in the column directly above the dividend's point. Then I repeat the same four steps I always use: DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, SUBTRACT, BRING DOWN.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Decimals is moving the decimal point in the divisor but forgetting to move it the same number of places in the dividend. For example, in 6.4 ÷ 0.8 a student changes 0.8 to 8 but leaves the dividend as 6.4, then divides 6.4 ÷ 8 = 0.8 instead of moving both points to get 64 ÷ 8 = 8. A second version of this mistake happens when the divisor has two decimal places, like 0.12: students move both points only 1 place instead of 2, turning 9.6 ÷ 0.12 into 96 ÷ 1.2 instead of the correct 960 ÷ 12. Count the divisor's decimal places first, then move BOTH points that same number of places.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To divide by a decimal, move its decimal point to the right until it is a whole number. Move the decimal point in the number you are dividing the same number of places. Then divide like whole numbers, and put the decimal point in the answer right above the new decimal point.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para dividir entre un decimal, mueve su punto decimal a la derecha hasta que sea un número entero. Mueve el punto decimal del número que estás dividiendo la misma cantidad de lugares. Luego divide como con números enteros y pon el punto decimal de la respuesta justo arriba del nuevo punto decimal.

lessons.title: Describe Data Using the Mean
lessons.objective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words mean, average, measure of center, balance point, and data set.

vocabulary.definition: The average of a data set. Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio de un conjunto de datos. Suma todos los valores y divide entre cuántos valores hay.

vocabulary.definition: Another word for the mean — the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Otra palabra para la media: la cantidad que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales.

vocabulary.definition: A single number used to describe the middle, or typical value, of a whole data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que se usa para describir el centro, o valor típico, de todo un conjunto de datos.

vocabulary.definition: The value where the total distance of the data above it equals the total distance below it. The mean is the balance point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor donde la distancia total de los datos por encima es igual a la distancia total por debajo. La media es el punto de equilibrio.

vocabulary.definition: The whole collection of values that were gathered or measured.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Toda la colección de valores que se recopilaron o midieron.

vocabulary.definition: The mean a person is trying to reach.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La media que una persona intenta alcanzar.

vocabulary.definition: The target mean times the number of values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La media objetivo multiplicada por la cantidad de valores.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Miguel's 4 days of earnings are shown with counters. When I combine all of the counters, there are 60 of them, which means Miguel earned $60 in all.
Now I redistribute the 60 counters equally among the 4 days. Each of the 4 groups ends up with 15 counters.
The arithmetic does exactly the same thing: I find the total, 60, and divide it by the number of days, 4. So 60 ÷ 4 = 15.
We can use $15 to describe Miguel's typical daily earnings. That leveled value is the mean.
instructional.commonMistake: The most common mistake with the mean is adding correctly and then dividing by the wrong number — or not dividing at all. Students report the total (for 8, 10, 6, 12 they say the mean is 36) or they divide by a count that does not match the data, such as dividing a 4-value total by 5, or skipping a zero when counting the values. Before you finish, do two things: count the values in the data set out loud, and check that your mean lands between the smallest and largest value. A mean of 36 for data that never goes above 12 is impossible.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: The mean (or average) is what each value would be if the total were shared equally. To find it, add all the numbers, then divide by how many numbers there are: mean = total ÷ how many numbers.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: La media (o promedio) es lo que valdría cada dato si el total se repartiera en partes iguales. Para hallarla, suma todos los números y luego divide entre cuántos números hay: media = total ÷ cuántos números hay.

lessons.title: Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation
lessons.objective: I can find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) to describe how spread out data is.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words mean absolute deviation, deviation, absolute value, and spread.

vocabulary.definition: The average distance of data values from the mean; it describes spread.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia promedio de los valores de datos respecto a la media; describe la dispersión.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from the mean.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de la media.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from zero. It is never negative.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de cero. Nunca es negativo.

vocabulary.definition: How far apart the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: The total shared equally among all the values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El total repartido en partes iguales entre todos los valores.

vocabulary.definition: How much the values in a data set differ from one another.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto difieren entre sí los valores de un conjunto de datos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My data set: 6, 8, 10, 12. First I find the mean: 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 = 36, then 36 ÷ 4 = 9. The mean is 9.
Next I find each deviation (value − mean): 6−9 = −3, 8−9 = −1, 10−9 = 1, 12−9 = 3.
Then I take the absolute value of each (the distance, never negative (zero is allowed)): 3, 1, 1, 3.
Finally I average those distances: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8, then 8 ÷ 4 = 2. So the MAD = 2 points.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Mean Absolute Deviation is adding the signed deviations (value − mean) instead of their absolute values, so the positives and negatives cancel out to 0. For 6, 8, 10, 12 (mean = 9), the deviations are −3, −1, 1, 3 — they sum to 0, but that is NOT the MAD. Before averaging, take the absolute value of every deviation so each becomes a nonnegative distance, including zero: |−3| = 3, |−1| = 1, |1| = 1, |3| = 3. Sum = 8, so MAD = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. A MAD of exactly 0 is a warning sign — it only happens if every value in the data set equals the mean.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: The mean absolute deviation (MAD) tells how spread out the data is. Find the mean, find how far each number is from the mean, then find the average of those distances. A small MAD means the numbers are close together; a large MAD means they are spread out.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: La desviación media absoluta dice qué tan separados están los datos. Halla la media, halla qué tan lejos está cada número de la media y luego halla el promedio de esas distancias. Si la desviación media absoluta es pequeña, los números están cerca unos de otros; si es grande, están muy separados.

lessons.title: Choose Appropriate Measures
lessons.objective: I can choose the best measure of center for a data set based on its shape.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my choice using the words mean, median, outlier, and skewed.

vocabulary.definition: A mean, median, or mode chosen because it describes a data set fairly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una media, mediana o moda elegida porque describe un conjunto de datos de manera justa.

vocabulary.definition: The average. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio. Suma todos los números y divide entre cuántos hay.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.

vocabulary.definition: When most data sits on one side with a tail on the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando la mayoría de los datos está de un lado con una cola del otro.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.

vocabulary.definition: Values bunched close together in one part of a display.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Valores agrupados muy cerca en una parte de la representación.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My data, the top scorer's points: 22, 24, 20, 25, 23, 21, 58. I notice 58 is much bigger than the rest, so it is an outlier.
Median: in order they are 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 58. The middle (4th) value is 23.
The mean (27.6) is higher than 6 of the 7 games because 58 pulled it up. So the median (23) better shows a typical game.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Appropriate Measures is defaulting to the mean just because "it uses all the data," without first checking whether an outlier or skewed shape is present. For example, given a player's points per game 14, 16, 15, 17, 16, 58, a student calculates the mean (136 ÷ 6 ≈ 22.7) and reports that as the typical game — but 58 is far from the cluster of 14–17, so it pulls the mean above 5 of the 6 games. The median (16) actually represents a typical game here. Before choosing a measure, always scan the data for an outlier or a long tail first: only use the mean once you've confirmed the data has neither.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: If the data has no outliers (numbers far from the rest), use the mean and the mean absolute deviation (MAD) to describe it. If the data has outliers or leans to one side, use the median and the interquartile range (IQR), because an outlier pulls the mean away from most of the numbers. To compare two data sets, look at both the typical value and the spread.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Si los datos no tienen valores atípicos (números muy lejos del resto), usa la media y la desviación media absoluta para describirlos. Si los datos tienen valores atípicos o están cargados hacia un lado, usa la mediana y el rango intercuartílico, porque un valor atípico jala la media lejos de la mayoría de los números. Para comparar dos conjuntos de datos, mira tanto el valor típico como la dispersión.

lessons.title: Add and Subtract Decimals
lessons.objective: I can add and subtract decimals by lining up the place values and the decimal points.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words decimal, place value, tenths, hundredths, and add zeros.

vocabulary.definition: Combine or find the difference between decimals by lining up equal place values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Combinar o hallar la diferencia entre decimales alineando valores posicionales iguales.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.

vocabulary.definition: What a digit is worth based on where it sits in a number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que vale un dígito según el lugar que ocupa en el número.

vocabulary.definition: The first spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 10.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El primer lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 10.

vocabulary.definition: The second spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El segundo lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 100.

vocabulary.definition: Adding zeros at the end of a decimal so numbers line up evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Agregar ceros al final de un decimal para que los números se alineen.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The tank has 128.75 liters. A shuttle adds 46.8 liters. I line up the decimal points and annex a zero: 46.80.
Now the thrusters use 19.35 liters, so I subtract: 175.55 − 19.35 = 156.20.
The final fuel level is 156.20 liters. I check with estimation: about 130 + 47 − 19 = 158, which is close, so my answer is reasonable.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Add and Subtract Decimals is lining up the last digits (the right edges) of each number instead of lining up the decimal points — for example, adding 8.3 and 2.45 as if the 3 and the 5 belong in the same column. Before you add or subtract, add zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places (write 8.3 as 8.30), then check that the decimal points sit directly above one another.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points so the same places match up. If one number has fewer digits after the point, write zeros at the end, like 4.5 = 4.50. Then add or subtract from right to left, and bring the decimal point straight down into the answer.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para sumar o restar decimales, alinea los puntos decimales para que coincidan los mismos lugares. Si un número tiene menos dígitos después del punto, escribe ceros al final, como 4.5 = 4.50. Luego suma o resta de derecha a izquierda y baja el punto decimal en línea recta hasta la respuesta.

lessons.title: Multiply Decimals
lessons.objective: I can multiply decimals and place the decimal point correctly in the product.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words product, decimal point, estimate, and decimal places.

vocabulary.definition: Find the product of decimals, then use place value to place the decimal point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar el producto de decimales y luego usar el valor posicional para colocar el punto decimal.

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you multiply.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando multiplicas.

vocabulary.definition: The dot that splits the whole number from the part after it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El punto que separa el número entero de la parte que sigue.

vocabulary.definition: A close answer you get by rounding first.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta cercana que obtienes al redondear primero.

vocabulary.definition: What a digit is worth based on where it sits in a number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que vale un dígito según el lugar que ocupa en el número.

vocabulary.definition: How many digits come after the decimal point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuántos dígitos hay después del punto decimal.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I want 4.5 × 12.60, the cost of 4.5 meters at $12.60 each.
First I multiply without points, like whole numbers: 45 × 1260 = 56,700.
Now I count decimal places: 4.5 has 1, and 12.60 has 2, so 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places.
I put the point 3 places from the right in 56,700: that gives 56.700, or $56.70.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Multiply Decimals is counting decimal places from only one factor instead of adding the decimal places from BOTH factors. For example, in 0.4 × 0.06, a student multiplies 4 × 6 = 24, then places the decimal point using just one factor's place count (1 place), writing 0.24 instead of the correct answer: 0.4 has 1 decimal place and 0.06 has 2 decimal places, for a total of 3, so 24 becomes 0.024. Before you submit, count the decimal places in EACH factor separately and add them together — that total is how many decimal places belong in your final answer.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To multiply decimals, first multiply as if there were no decimal points. Then count how many digits come after the decimal point in both numbers together. Put the decimal point in the answer so it has that same number of digits after the point.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para multiplicar decimales, primero multiplica como si no hubiera puntos decimales. Luego cuenta cuántos dígitos hay después del punto decimal en los dos números juntos. Pon el punto decimal en la respuesta para que tenga esa misma cantidad de dígitos después del punto.

lessons.title: Understand Ratios
lessons.objective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain a comparison using the words ratio, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and colon notation.

vocabulary.definition: Use a ratio to compare two quantities by division.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una razón para comparar dos cantidades mediante la división.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.

vocabulary.definition: Looking at two or more amounts to see how they are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar dos o más cantidades para ver cómo se relacionan.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing one part of a group to another part.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una parte de un grupo con otra parte.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing one part to the whole group.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una parte con todo el grupo.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a ratio with two dots between the numbers, like 3:2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con dos puntos entre los números, como 3:2.

vocabulary.definition: A bar cut into equal parts that shows how two amounts in a ratio compare, and how they make up the whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una barra dividida en partes iguales que muestra cómo se comparan dos cantidades de una razón y cómo forman el total.

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines lined up so matching tick marks show the two quantities in a ratio at the same time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas numéricas alineadas para que las marcas correspondientes muestren las dos cantidades de una razón al mismo tiempo.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Chef Reyes uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water.
I am comparing two amounts: apple juice and sparkling water.
I write apple juice to sparkling water, in that order, as 3 to 2, or 3:2.
I can also draw the ratio. On a tape diagram I give apple juice 3 equal parts and sparkling water 2 equal parts, so one batch is 5 parts in all.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Understand Ratios is writing the ratio in the wrong order: when asked for the ratio of apple juice to sparkling water in a recipe that uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water, some students write 2:3 (sparkling water to apple juice) because they list the ingredients in whatever order comes to mind rather than the order the question asks for. The two ratios describe different drinks — 3:2 means 3 cups of juice for every 2 cups of water, while 2:3 would mean only 2 cups of juice for every 3 cups of water. Always match the order of your ratio to the order named in the question: "apple juice to sparkling water" means the apple juice number comes first, giving 3:2.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A ratio compares two amounts, like 3 cups of apple juice to 2 cups of water. The order matters: 3 to 2 is not the same as 2 to 3. A ratio can compare one part to another part, or one part to the whole group.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades, como 3 tazas de jugo de manzana por 2 tazas de agua. El orden importa: 3 a 2 no es lo mismo que 2 a 3. Una razón puede comparar una parte con otra parte, o una parte con todo el grupo.

lessons.title: Understand Rates and Unit Rates
lessons.objective: I can describe a rate using its two different units and use a model to find a travel time, and I can find a unit rate to compare prices and decide the better buy.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain a rate like "150 miles per hour" using distance and time units, and explain my choice using the words rate, unit rate, per, and better buy.

vocabulary.definition: A rate compares different units; a unit rate compares a quantity to 1 unit.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa compara unidades diferentes; una tasa unitaria compara una cantidad con 1 unidad.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.

vocabulary.definition: For each one. Example: 5 dollars per book.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Por cada uno. Ejemplo: 5 dólares por libro.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.

vocabulary.definition: A unit rate that gives the cost of exactly 1 item, like $0.60 per game.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa unitaria que da el costo de exactamente 1 artículo, como $0.60 por juego.

vocabulary.definition: The choice that costs less for each item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La opción que cuesta menos por cada artículo.

vocabulary.definition: Splitting a total into equal groups.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Repartir un total en grupos iguales.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Booth A charges $3 for 5 games. I want the cost for just 1 game.
I divide the cost by the games: $3 ÷ 5 = $0.60.
So Booth A costs $0.60 per game. That is the unit rate.
Because this unit rate is money for one item, it has its own name: it is the unit price.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Rates and Unit Rates is comparing total costs instead of unit rates: a student sees Pack X at $4.00 for 10 tokens and Pack Y at $6.00 for 16 tokens and picks Pack X just because $4.00 is the smaller number, without dividing to find the cost per token ($0.40 for Pack X vs. $0.375 for Pack Y — Pack Y is actually the better buy). A second common mistake is dividing backwards — finding tokens ÷ cost instead of cost ÷ tokens — which turns 'dollars per token' into 'tokens per dollar' and gives an answer that looks reasonable but answers the wrong question. Always divide the total cost by the number of items, and check that your unit rate answers 'the cost for ONE item,' not the reverse.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A rate compares two amounts with different units, like $12 for 3 pounds. A unit rate is the amount for just 1, like $4 for 1 pound. To find it, divide: $12 ÷ 3 = $4.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una tasa compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como $12 por 3 libras. Una tasa unitaria es la cantidad por solo 1, como $4 por 1 libra. Para hallarla, divide: $12 ÷ 3 = $4.

lessons.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Tables
lessons.objective: I can use a ratio table to find equivalent ratios.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my table using the words ratio table, equivalent ratio, scale factor, and pattern.

vocabulary.definition: Tables that organize pairs of equivalent ratios.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tablas que organizan pares de razones equivalentes.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that shows a pattern.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que muestra un patrón.

vocabulary.definition: Two ratios that mean the same thing, like 1:2 and 2:4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos razones que significan lo mismo, como 1:2 y 2:4.

vocabulary.definition: The number you multiply both parts of a ratio by to get an equal ratio.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número por el que multiplicas ambas partes de una razón para obtener una razón igual.

vocabulary.definition: A rule that numbers follow again and again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla que los números siguen una y otra vez.

vocabulary.definition: Building new rows of a ratio table by adding each column's own constant amount, so the two columns grow together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Formar nuevas filas de una tabla de razones sumando a cada columna su propia cantidad constante, para que las dos columnas crezcan juntas.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that use different numbers but compare the same way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que usan números diferentes pero comparan de la misma manera.

vocabulary.definition: Divide both terms of a ratio by the same number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dividir ambos términos de una razón entre el mismo número.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The pancake recipe is 2 cups of mix for every 3 cups of milk, so the ratio is 2:3.
To make 2 batches, my scale factor is 2.
I multiply both numbers by 2: 2 x 2 = 4 cups of mix, and 3 x 2 = 6 cups of milk.
Now my row is 4:6, which is the same ratio as 2:3.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Ratio Tables is scaling only ONE part of the ratio, or adding the scale factor to a part instead of multiplying by it — for example, turning 2:3 into 6:3 (multiplying only the first number by 3 and forgetting the second) or into 4:5 (adding the scale factor 2 to the second number instead of multiplying, since 3+2=5 but 3×2=6). Before you submit, multiply BOTH numbers by the same scale factor and check that your new ratio simplifies back to the original.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To make an equal ratio, multiply or divide both numbers by the same number. A ratio table lists these equal ratios in rows. Look for the pattern down each column to fill in missing numbers.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para formar una razón igual, multiplica o divide los dos números por el mismo número. Una tabla de razones muestra estas razones iguales en filas. Busca el patrón en cada columna para completar los números que faltan.

lessons.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs
lessons.objective: I can graph the values from a ratio table as points on the coordinate plane.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my graph using the words coordinate plane, ordered pair, origin, and proportional.

vocabulary.definition: Plot the paired values from a ratio table as ordered pairs.
vocabulary.termEs: Representar tablas de razones en una gráfica
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ubicar los valores emparejados de una tabla de razones como pares ordenados.

vocabulary.definition: A grid with a line going across and a line going up to plot points.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula con una línea horizontal y una vertical para marcar puntos.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers (x, y) that tell where a point is on a grid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números (x, y) que dicen dónde está un punto en una cuadrícula.

vocabulary.definition: Points that make a straight line on a grid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puntos que forman una línea recta en una cuadrícula.

vocabulary.definition: Two amounts that grow together at the same rate.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos cantidades que crecen juntas al mismo ritmo.

vocabulary.definition: The point (0, 0) where the two grid lines cross.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El punto (0, 0) donde se cruzan las dos líneas de la cuadrícula.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that shows a pattern.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que muestra un patrón.

vocabulary.definition: The point (1, r) on a graph, where r is the amount for one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El punto (1, r) en una gráfica, donde r es la cantidad que corresponde a uno.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The recipe uses 2 ounces of sauce for every 1 sundae.
I put sundaes on the x-axis and ounces of sauce on the y-axis.
For 1 sundae I need 2 ounces, so I plot the ordered pair (1, 2): right 1, up 2.
For 2 sundaes I need 4 ounces, so I plot (2, 4): right 2, up 4.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Graph Ratio Tables is writing the ordered pair in the wrong order — putting the second table value first instead of matching (x, y) to the table's column order. For example, if a recipe table shows 2 cups of sugar for every 4 cups of flour, a student might plot (4, 2) instead of (2, 4), landing the point in a completely different spot on the grid. Before you plot, check: which quantity goes on the x-axis, and does your ordered pair start with that number?
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Each row of a ratio table gives a pair of numbers (x, y) that you can plot as a point on a graph. When the ratios are equal, the points line up in a straight line that goes through (0, 0).
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Cada fila de una tabla de razones da un par de números (x, y) que puedes marcar como un punto en una gráfica. Cuando las razones son iguales, los puntos quedan en una línea recta que pasa por (0, 0).

lessons.title: Compare Ratio Relationships
lessons.objective: I can compare ratios by finding unit rates or using equivalent ratios.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my comparison using the words unit rate, equivalent ratio, compare, and common denominator.

vocabulary.definition: Decide which ratio is greater, less, or equal by using equivalent ratios or unit rates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Decidir cuál razón es mayor, menor o igual usando razones equivalentes o tasas unitarias.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.

vocabulary.definition: Two ratios that mean the same thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos razones que significan lo mismo.

vocabulary.definition: To look at ratios and see which is bigger, smaller, or equal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar razones para ver cuál es mayor, menor o igual.

vocabulary.definition: To write a ratio with smaller numbers that still compares the same way. 6:8 and 3:4 are the same ratio.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con números más pequeños que compara igual. 6:8 y 3:4 son la misma razón.

vocabulary.definition: A bottom number that two fractions can share so you can compare them.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número de abajo que dos fracciones pueden compartir para compararlas.

vocabulary.definition: A number that both terms can be scaled to.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número al que ambos términos pueden escalarse.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest common multiple of two numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El menor múltiplo común de dos números.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Chef Reyes uses 3 tbsp cocoa for 5 oz milk (3:5). Chef Tran uses 4 tbsp for 7 oz milk (4:7).
I cannot compare yet because the milk amounts are different.
I scale both to 35 oz of milk. For Reyes: 5 x 7 = 35, so 3 x 7 = 21 tbsp, giving 21:35.
For Tran: 7 x 5 = 35, so 4 x 5 = 20 tbsp, giving 20:35.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Compare Ratios is thinking the ratio with the bigger raw number automatically wins — like assuming Chef Tran's 8 tablespoons of cocoa must be more chocolatey than Chef Reyes's 6 tablespoons, without checking that the milk amounts (14 oz vs. 10 oz) are different. Never compare the raw numbers alone — always scale both ratios to the same amount or find each unit rate first.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To compare two ratios fairly, find the amount for just 1 of each, like the price for 1 item. Or change both ratios so one of their numbers is the same. Then you can see which is the better buy or the faster speed.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para comparar dos razones de forma justa, halla la cantidad por solo 1 en cada una, como el precio de 1 artículo. O cambia las dos razones para que uno de sus números sea igual. Así puedes ver cuál es la mejor compra o la mayor rapidez.

lessons.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements within the Same System
lessons.objective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert between units within the same measurement system.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain a conversion using the words unit ratio, convert, measurement system, and per.

vocabulary.term: Convert Measurements within the Same System
vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a measurement in a different unit of the SAME system, such as feet into inches or liters into milliliters.
vocabulary.termEs: Convertir medidas dentro del mismo sistema
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida en otra unidad del MISMO sistema, como pies a pulgadas o litros a mililitros.

vocabulary.definition: The ratio that links two units in the same measurement system, such as 12 inches to 1 foot. Within one system it is exact.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La razón que relaciona dos unidades del mismo sistema de medición, como 12 pulgadas a 1 pie. Dentro de un mismo sistema es exacta.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares an amount to exactly 1 unit of another quantity, like 12 inches to 1 foot.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una cantidad con exactamente 1 unidad de otra cantidad, como 12 pulgadas por 1 pie.

vocabulary.definition: To change a measurement from one unit to another without changing how much it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cambiar una medida de una unidad a otra sin cambiar la cantidad que representa.

vocabulary.definition: A family of units that go together — customary units like inches and feet, or metric units like milliliters and liters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una familia de unidades que van juntas: unidades usuales como pulgadas y pies, o métricas como mililitros y litros.

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines lined up so matching tick marks show two units for the same amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas numéricas alineadas para que las marcas correspondientes muestren dos unidades de la misma cantidad.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that lets you scale a conversion up or down one row at a time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que permite escalar una conversión hacia arriba o hacia abajo fila por fila.

vocabulary.definition: The U.S. system of units: inch, foot, yard, mile, ounce, pound, cup, quart, gallon.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El sistema de unidades de EE. UU.: pulgada, pie, yarda, milla, onza, libra, taza, cuarto, galón.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A ride requires riders to be at or above 44 inches tall. A child is 4 feet tall. The two measurements use different units, so I cannot compare them yet.

Both units belong to the customary system, and there are 12 inches in one foot. That relationship is the conversion factor. As a ratio it is 12 : 1 — a unit ratio, because it compares an amount to exactly 1 foot.
Inches are smaller than feet, so there will be MORE of them: I multiply. 4 × 12 = 48.
The child is 48 inches tall. Now the comparison is fair: 48 inches is greater than 44 inches, so the child can go on the ride.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake when converting within a measurement system is choosing the operation by habit instead of by unit size — multiplying every time. Converting 36 inches to feet by multiplying gives 36 × 12 = 432 feet, taller than a 40-story building. Ask first which unit is smaller: it takes MORE small units to make the same amount, so going to a smaller unit multiplies, and going to a larger unit divides.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To change units, use how the two units are related, like 1 foot = 12 inches. When you go from a bigger unit to a smaller unit, multiply. When you go from a smaller unit to a bigger unit, divide.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para cambiar de unidad, usa cómo se relacionan las dos unidades, como 1 pie = 12 pulgadas. Cuando pasas de una unidad más grande a una más pequeña, multiplica. Cuando pasas de una unidad más pequeña a una más grande, divide.

lessons.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems
lessons.objective: I can use ratio reasoning to convert measurements between the customary and metric systems.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain a conversion between systems using the words conversion factor, approximately, customary, and metric.

vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a customary measurement as a metric one, or the reverse, so two amounts can be compared.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida usual como métrica, o al revés, para poder comparar dos cantidades.

vocabulary.definition: The ratio that links a unit in one system to a unit in the other, such as 1 mile to about 1.609 kilometers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La razón que relaciona una unidad de un sistema con una del otro, como 1 milla a unos 1.609 kilómetros.

vocabulary.definition: The measurement system used in the United States: inches, feet, miles, ounces, pounds, cups, quarts, gallons.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El sistema de medidas que se usa en Estados Unidos: pulgadas, pies, millas, onzas, libras, tazas, cuartos y galones.

vocabulary.definition: The measurement system used in most of the world, built on tens: centimeters, meters, kilometers, grams, kilograms, liters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El sistema de medidas que se usa en casi todo el mundo, basado en decenas: centímetros, metros, kilómetros, gramos, kilogramos y litros.

vocabulary.definition: Close to, but not exactly equal. A rounded conversion factor gives an approximate result, written with ≈; an exact conversion uses =.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cercano, pero no exactamente igual. Un factor de conversión redondeado da un resultado aproximado, escrito con ≈; una conversión exacta usa =.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios used to scale a conversion factor up to the amount you actually need.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que sirve para escalar un factor de conversión hasta la cantidad que necesitas.

vocabulary.definition: Checking that the size of an answer makes sense for the situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Comprobar que el tamaño de una respuesta tiene sentido para la situación.

vocabulary.definition: A problem that needs two or more operations done in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un problema que necesita dos o más operaciones hechas en orden.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Evelyn sees a Canadian highway sign reading 100 kilometers per hour and wonders whether that is faster or slower than 100 miles per hour.
Kilometers are metric and miles are customary, so 100 and 100 cannot be compared as they stand. Both measure distance, so a conversion factor links them: 1 kilometer ≈ 0.6 mile, or the ratio 1 : 0.6.
I build a ratio table from that unit ratio. Kilometers 1, 10, 100 pair with miles 0.6, 6, 60 — each column multiplies both numbers by the same factor.
So 100 kilometers ≈ 60 miles, which means 100 kilometers per hour ≈ 60 miles per hour.
instructional.commonMistake: Compare measurements only after converting to a common unit. Also check whether the conversion factor is exact or rounded: 1 inch = 2.54 cm and 1 international mile = 1.609344 km are exact; 1 mile ≈ 1.609 km is rounded. Use ≈ when the factor or the result has been rounded.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Some units come from different systems, like inches and centimeters, or pounds and kilograms. A conversion fact links them, like 1 kilogram is about 2.2 pounds. Use a ratio table, or multiply or divide by that number, to find the same amount in the other unit.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Algunas unidades vienen de sistemas distintos, como las pulgadas y los centímetros, o las libras y los kilogramos. Un dato de conversión las une, como que 1 kilogramo es más o menos 2.2 libras. Usa una tabla de razones, o multiplica o divide por ese número, para hallar la misma cantidad en la otra unidad.
