lessons.title: Solve Problems with Unit Rates
lessons.objective: I can solve real-world problems by using unit rates to compare options.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my comparison using the words unit rate, better buy, per unit, and rate.

vocabulary.definition: Find an amount per 1 unit and use it to compare choices or solve a problem.
vocabulary.termEs: Resolución de problemas con tasas unitarias
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar una cantidad por 1 unidad y usarla para comparar opciones o resolver un problema.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.

vocabulary.definition: The choice that costs less for each item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La opción que cuesta menos por cada artículo.

vocabulary.definition: Looking at two or more amounts to see how they are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar dos o más cantidades para ver cómo se relacionan.

vocabulary.definition: For each single item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Por cada artículo.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence saying two ratios are equal. It helps find a missing number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática que dice que dos razones son iguales. Ayuda a hallar un número que falta.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Fun Supply Co. sells 500 tokens for $60. I want the cost for 1 token.
I divide the price by the tokens: $60 ÷ 500 = $0.12.
So this deal is $0.12 per token. That is the unit rate.
Now I can compare it fairly to a deal with a different number of tokens.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Solve Problems with Unit Rates is comparing the total prices instead of the cost per item — the deal with the smaller total can still cost more per unit. Always reduce each option to its unit rate before you decide, then pick the lower one.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A unit rate is the cost for just 1 item. Find it by dividing the total cost by the number of items. Compare unit rates to find the best deal, and multiply the unit rate by how many you want to find the total cost.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una tasa unitaria es el costo de solo 1 artículo. Hállala dividiendo el costo total entre el número de artículos. Compara las tasas unitarias para hallar la mejor oferta, y multiplica la tasa unitaria por cuántos quieres para hallar el costo total.

lessons.title: Equivalent Ratios
lessons.objective: I can find and check equivalent ratios using multiplication and division.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words equivalent ratios, rate, proportion, and simplify.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that compare quantities in the same relationship.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que comparan cantidades en la misma relación.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing two amounts with different units, like miles per hour.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara dos cantidades con unidades distintas, como millas por hora.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence saying two ratios are equal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática que dice que dos razones son iguales.

vocabulary.definition: To write a ratio with smaller numbers that still compares the same way. 6:8 and 3:4 are the same ratio.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con números más pequeños que compara igual. 6:8 y 3:4 son la misma razón.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that shows a pattern.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que muestra un patrón.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Chef Montoya's soup serves 8 people, but she needs to serve 32.
I find the scale factor: 32 divided by 8 = 4.
The recipe uses 3 cups of tomatoes to 2 cups of broth, a 3:2 ratio.
I multiply both by 4: 3 x 4 = 12 cups of tomatoes, and 2 x 4 = 8 cups of broth.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equivalent Ratios is ADDING the scale factor to one part instead of MULTIPLYING both parts by it. For example, scaling 2:5 by a factor of 4 should give 8:20 (2×4 and 5×4) — not 6:9 (2+4 and 5+4). Adding changes the taste of the recipe (and the value of the ratio); only multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same amount keeps it equivalent.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Equivalent ratios are equal ratios, like 1:2 and 3:6. To find a missing number, find what one number was multiplied or divided by, then do the same thing to the other number.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Las razones equivalentes son razones iguales, como 1:2 y 3:6. Para hallar un número que falta, busca por cuánto se multiplicó o dividió uno de los números, y luego haz lo mismo con el otro número.

lessons.title: Convert Measurement Units
lessons.objective: I can convert measurement units using ratios and conversion factors.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my conversion using the words conversion factor, unit, equivalent, and ratio.

vocabulary.definition: Rename a measurement in a different unit without changing its amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresar una medida en una unidad diferente sin cambiar su cantidad.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that helps you change one unit into another.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que te ayuda a cambiar una unidad por otra.

vocabulary.definition: A standard amount used to measure, like an inch or a liter.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad estándar para medir, como una pulgada o un litro.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just in different units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, solo en unidades distintas.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.

vocabulary.definition: The U.S. way of measuring, like inches, feet, and pounds.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La forma de medir de EE. UU., como pulgadas, pies y libras.

vocabulary.definition: A way of measuring by 10s, like meters, liters, and grams.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma de medir de 10 en 10, como metros, litros y gramos.

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that shows a pattern.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que muestra un patrón.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The cabinet is 5 feet tall. I want to know how many inches that is.
My conversion factor is 1 foot = 12 inches.
Inches are smaller than feet, so I multiply: 5 × 12 = 60.
So 5 feet = 60 inches.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To change units, write the amount as a fraction over 1. Then multiply by a conversion fact, like 12 inches over 1 foot, set up so the unit you start with cancels out. Multiply across the top and the bottom, and the new unit is what is left.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para cambiar de unidad, escribe la cantidad como una fracción sobre 1. Luego multiplica por un dato de conversión, como 12 pulgadas sobre 1 pie, acomodado para que la unidad con la que empiezas se cancele. Multiplica los números de arriba y los de abajo, y la unidad nueva es la que queda.

lessons.title: Understand Percent
lessons.objective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain what a percent means using the words per hundred, part, whole, and equivalent ratio.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100, así que todo porcentaje responde “¿cuántos de cada 100?”

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares a number to 100. The word means “per hundred,” and the symbol is %.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. La palabra significa “por cada cien” y su símbolo es %.

vocabulary.definition: The meaning hidden inside the word percent: for every group of 100. It is why every percent can be written as a fraction over 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El significado dentro de la palabra porcentaje: por cada grupo de 100. Por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como fracción sobre 100.

vocabulary.definition: A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares. Shading squares shows a percent directly, one square per percent.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula de 10 por 10 con 100 cuadros. Sombrear cuadros muestra un porcentaje directamente, un cuadro por cada uno por ciento.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of one part against the whole amount. In a percent, the whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de una parte con el total. En un porcentaje, el total siempre es 100 %.

vocabulary.definition: More than one whole. A percent above 100 means the amount is larger than the thing it is being compared to.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Más de un entero. Un porcentaje mayor que 100 significa que la cantidad es mayor que aquello con lo que se compara.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio with the same value, made by multiplying or dividing both terms by the same number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón con el mismo valor, formada al multiplicar o dividir ambos términos por el mismo número.

vocabulary.definition: A bar split into equal parts to show a percent.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una barra dividida en partes iguales para mostrar un porcentaje.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Students voted on a mascot, and 4 out of every 10 voters chose the tiger. I want to know how many that is out of 100.
"4 out of every 10" is a ratio, so I write an equivalent ratio with 100 as the second term. Multiplying both terms by 10 gives 40 out of 100.
On a decimal grid of 100 squares, I shade 40 squares — one square for each percent.
40 out of 100 is written 40%. So 40% of the students voted for the tiger.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake with percent is scaling only one term of the ratio: reading 7 out of 10 as 7%. A percent compares to 100, so BOTH terms must be multiplied by the same factor — 10 × 10 = 100, so 7 × 10 = 70, giving 70%. Reading it as 7% describes seats that are nearly empty when they are nearly full. A second mistake is treating a percent as an amount: 150% of a 200-point goal is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points, not 150 points.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A percent tells how many out of 100. For example, 4 out of 10 is 40 out of 100, or 40%.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un porcentaje indica cuántos hay de cada 100. Por ejemplo, 4 de cada 10 son 40 de cada 100, o 40%.

lessons.title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
lessons.objective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my conversions using the words percent, decimal, equivalent, and benchmark.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just written a different way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, escrito de otra forma.

vocabulary.definition: A familiar number you use to guess, like 50% or 1/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número conocido que usas para estimar, como 50% o 1/2.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.

vocabulary.definition: The second place after the decimal point; parts out of 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La segunda posición después del punto decimal; partes de 100.

vocabulary.definition: One form, such as percents, that every value in a list is rewritten in.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma, como porcentajes, en la que se reescriben todos los valores de una lista.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A player scored 3/4 of the points. Percent means out of 100, so I want an equivalent fraction with 100 on the bottom.
What do I multiply the denominator 4 by to get 100? 4 × 25 = 100, so my scale factor is 25.
I have to multiply the top by that same 25: 3 × 25 = 75. So 3/4 = 75/100.
75 out of 100 is 75%. And 75/100 as a decimal is 0.75, because hundredths sit two places after the point.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents is treating the numerator and denominator as the percent's digits — turning 3/5 into "35%" by just reading the 3 and the 5. Percent means out of 100, so the fix is to build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too — 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%. A second version of this mistake is scaling only ONE part of the fraction (writing 3/5 = 3/100 or 60/5). Whatever you multiply the denominator by, you must multiply the numerator by the same number. When a denominator will not reach 100 evenly (8, 3, 7), divide the numerator by the denominator instead and then multiply by 100.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: One amount can be written as a fraction, decimal, or percent. One quarter is 1/4, 0.25, and 25%.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una misma cantidad se puede escribir como fracción, decimal o porcentaje. Un cuarto es 1/4, 0.25 y 25%.

lessons.title: Estimate the Percent of a Number
lessons.objective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain an estimate using the words about, benchmark, and compatible numbers.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, found without exact computation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin cálculo exacto.

vocabulary.definition: A friendly percent — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — used as a landmark for estimating.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje amigable — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — que sirve de punto de referencia.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with mentally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números cercanos a los originales con los que es fácil calcular mentalmente.

vocabulary.definition: Two parallel number lines that pair amounts with their percents at the same positions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas paralelas que emparejan cantidades con sus porcentajes en las mismas posiciones.

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem — and it can change between questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que representa el 100% en un problema, y puede cambiar entre preguntas.

vocabulary.definition: Break a percent into friendly pieces that are easy to find.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un porcentaje en partes fáciles de calcular.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The whole is 6 GB — that is 100%.
I mark the bottom line in benchmark jumps of 25%: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%.
Equivalent ratios give the top line: 25% of 6 GB is 1.5 GB, so the top reads 0, 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6.
4 GB used lands between 4.5 (75%) and 3 (50%), close to 4.5 — so about 70% of the storage is used.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's estimate the metal recycling together
instructional.commonMistake: Keeping the same whole for every question — when the problem says 'of the used storage,' the whole changes from 6 GB to 4 GB, and estimates anchored to the old whole are wrong before any arithmetic happens.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: For a quick estimate, use friendly numbers: 19% of 412 is about 20% of 400, or 80.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para estimar rápidamente, usa números fáciles: 19% de 412 es aproximadamente 20% de 400, o 80.

lessons.title: Find and Compare with Percentages
lessons.objective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words percent, base, part, and equation.

vocabulary.definition: A part of a number found by multiplying the number by the percent written as a decimal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una parte de un número que se halla multiplicando el número por el porcentaje escrito como decimal.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.

vocabulary.definition: The whole amount you start with — the number right after the word “of.”
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad total con la que empiezas: el número que va después de la palabra “de”.

vocabulary.definition: How much of the base (the whole) you get. It is your answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto obtienes de la base (el total). Es tu respuesta.

vocabulary.definition: A number sentence with an equal sign. The percent one is: part = percent × base.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración numérica con signo de igual. La de porcentaje es: parte = porcentaje × base.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines that line up percents with amounts.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas numéricas que alinean porcentajes con cantidades.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction with the same value written with different numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción con el mismo valor escrita con números diferentes.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The claw machine costs 60 tickets, and it is 25% off. I need 25% of 60.
Step 1 — find the base (the whole): the number after “of” is 60.
Step 2 — the percent as a decimal: 25% means 25 out of 100, so 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25.
Step 3 — multiply: 0.25 × 60 = 15.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Find the Percent of a Number is multiplying by the percent number itself instead of its decimal form — for example, finding 30% of 80 by computing 30 × 80 = 2,400 instead of 0.30 × 80 = 24. Always divide the percent by 100 to get the decimal, then multiply that decimal by the base.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A 25% discount means you save one quarter of the price. On an $80 item, that is $20 off, so you pay $60.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un descuento de 25% significa ahorrar un cuarto del precio. En un artículo de $80, el ahorro es $20 y pagas $60.

lessons.title: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
lessons.objective: I can determine the whole when I know a part and the percent that part represents.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain how I found the whole using the words part, whole, percent, and equation.

vocabulary.term: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
vocabulary.definition: Working backwards from a part and its percent to find the whole amount it came from.
vocabulary.termEs: Hallar el total dados la parte y el porcentaje
vocabulary.definitionEs: Trabajar al revés a partir de una parte y su porcentaje para hallar el total del que proviene.

vocabulary.definition: The amount you already know — the piece of the whole that the percent describes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que ya conoces: el pedazo del total que describe el porcentaje.

vocabulary.definition: The full amount the percent is measured against. The whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad completa contra la que se mide el porcentaje. El total siempre es 100 %.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines lined up — dollars on one, percents on the other — so matching marks show the same amount two ways.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas alineadas —dólares en una y porcentajes en la otra— para que las marcas correspondientes muestren la misma cantidad de dos formas.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign. Here it says percent × whole = part, with the whole unknown.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con signo de igual. Aquí dice porcentaje × total = parte, con el total desconocido.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing a number to 100. To compute with it, write it in decimal form: 60% = 0.6.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. Para calcular con él, escríbelo en forma decimal: 60 % = 0.6.

vocabulary.definition: The operation that undoes another operation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La operación que deshace otra operación.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Akela paid $42 for a sweater on sale, and that was 60% of the original price. The $42 is the part; the original price is the whole, which is 100%.
I put the matching values in a ratio table: 60% pairs with $42. I want a friendly 10% row, so I divide both values by 6: 10% pairs with $7.
To reach the whole, I multiply both values in the 10% row by 10: 100% pairs with $70. The original price is $70, which is larger than the sale price.
I can check the table with an equation: 0.6 × v = 42, so v = 42 ÷ 0.6 = 70. The equation describes the same part-to-whole relationship.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake when finding the whole is multiplying by the percent instead of dividing. For "$42 is 60% of the original price," computing 0.6 × 42 = $25.20 makes the original price SMALLER than the sale price — impossible for a discount. Since percent × whole = part, the whole is found by dividing: 42 ÷ 0.6 = $70. Whenever the percent is less than 100%, the whole must come out larger than the part, so a smaller answer is the tell.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: If $42 is 60% of a price, the full price is $70. The full amount represents 100%.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Si $42 representa el 60% de un precio, el precio total es $70. La cantidad total representa el 100%.

lessons.title: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain how I found the area using the words base, height, area, and formula.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un paralelogramo. Fórmula: A = b × h, usando la altura perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado que está inclinado en vez de subir y bajar verticalmente. No es la altura perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con dos pares de lados paralelos.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a parallelogram can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un paralelogramo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta hacia arriba desde la base hasta la parte de arriba.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I have a parallelogram with a base of 14 feet and a height of 9 feet.
I write the formula: A = base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = 14 × 9.
I multiply: 14 × 9 = 126.
instructional.commonMistake: The most common mistake in Area of Parallelograms is multiplying the base by the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height. For a parallelogram with a base of 16 ft, a perpendicular height of 9 ft, and a slanted side of 11 ft, students compute 16 × 11 = 176 square feet instead of the correct 16 × 9 = 144 square feet. The height must be the straight-up (perpendicular) distance between the base and its opposite side, not the length of the slanted side, even though the slanted side is often the number that 'looks' like it belongs in the formula.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To find the area of a parallelogram, multiply the base by the height. The height goes straight up from the base, not along the slanted side. Example: a base of 6 ft and a height of 4 ft gives 6 × 4 = 24 square feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para hallar el área de un paralelogramo, multiplica la base por la altura. La altura sube recta desde la base, no por el lado inclinado. Ejemplo: una base de 6 pies y una altura de 4 pies da 6 × 4 = 24 pies cuadrados.

lessons.title: Determine the Area of Triangles
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words base, height, area, and perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y altura, por eso A = ½ × b × h.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a triangle can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un triángulo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se unen formando una esquina recta (90 grados).

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My triangular garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I multiply base × height first: 12 × 8 = 96.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is forgetting the ½ — students multiply base × height like a rectangle and stop there, or they use the triangle's slanted side instead of the perpendicular height that's already given. Always check: did I take half, and did I use the straight-up height, not the slanted side?
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A triangle is half of a rectangle. To find its area, multiply the base by the height, then take half. A triangle with base 10 ft and height 6 ft has area 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30 square feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo. Para hallar su área, multiplica la base por la altura y luego toma la mitad. Un triángulo con base de 10 pies y altura de 6 pies tiene un área de 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30 pies cuadrados.

lessons.title: Determine the Area of Trapezoids
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a trapezoid using the formula A = ½(b1 + b2) × h.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words trapezoid, base, height, and area.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a trapezoid. Formula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un trapecio. Fórmula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with just one pair of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con solo un par de lados paralelos.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los dos lados paralelos de un trapecio.

vocabulary.definition: The other parallel side of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El otro lado paralelo de un trapecio.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance between the two parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta entre los dos lados paralelos.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My trapezoid window has a top base of 4 feet, a bottom base of 8 feet, and a height of 5 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
I add the bases first: 4 + 8 = 12.
I multiply by the height: 12 × 5 = 60.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Trapezoids is forgetting the ½ in A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. After adding the bases and multiplying by the height, students stop there instead of taking half — for example, with bases 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft, they compute (6 + 10) × 4 = 64 sq ft instead of taking half to get the correct 32 sq ft. That unhalved number is really the area of the parallelogram made from two trapezoids, not the area of one trapezoid. Before you submit, always ask: "Did I take half of my last answer?"
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A trapezoid has two parallel sides called bases. To find its area, add the two bases, multiply by the height, then take half. Bases 6 ft and 10 ft with height 4 ft: (6 + 10) × 4 ÷ 2 = 32 square feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un trapecio tiene dos lados paralelos llamados bases. Para hallar su área, suma las dos bases, multiplica por la altura y luego toma la mitad. Bases de 6 pies y 10 pies con altura de 4 pies: (6 + 10) × 4 ÷ 2 = 32 pies cuadrados.

lessons.title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a composite figure by decomposing it into basic shapes, including a regular polygon split into triangles, and adding or subtracting the areas.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words composite figure, decompose, add, and subtract.

vocabulary.definition: The total space inside a figure made of basic shapes. Formula: A = A₁ + A₂ — add the parts (or subtract a missing piece).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio total dentro de una figura formada por figuras básicas. Fórmula: A = A₁ + A₂ — suma las partes (o resta la pieza que falta).

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.

vocabulary.definition: To break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar una figura en figuras más pequeñas y simples.

vocabulary.definition: Add up the areas of the smaller shapes to get the total.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar las áreas de las figuras pequeñas para obtener el total.

vocabulary.definition: Take away the area of a missing piece from a bigger shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Quitar el área de una parte que falta de una figura más grande.

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.

vocabulary.definition: A shape whose sides are all the same length and whose angles are all the same size.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cuyos lados tienen la misma longitud y cuyos ángulos tienen la misma medida.

vocabulary.definition: Exactly the same size and shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Exactamente del mismo tamaño y forma.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My L-shaped room splits into two rectangles: one is 12 ft by 8 ft, the other is 6 ft by 5 ft.
First rectangle: A = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 square feet.
Second rectangle: A = 6 × 5 = 30 square feet.
The pieces are joined, so I add: 96 + 30 = 126.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Composite Figures is adding every piece even when a piece has been cut out of the figure. For a 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle with a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangular notch cut from one corner, students compute the full rectangle 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft and stop, or they add the notch instead of removing it (80 + 6 = 86 sq ft) instead of subtracting it: 80 − (3 × 2) = 80 − 6 = 74 sq ft. Before submitting, check whether each piece is part of the figure (add it) or missing from the figure (subtract it).
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A tricky shape can be split into simple shapes like rectangles and triangles. Find the area of each piece, then add them. If a piece is cut out, subtract it instead. An L-shaped room made of a 9 × 6 and a 7 × 3 rectangle has area 54 + 21 = 75 square feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una figura complicada se puede dividir en figuras simples como rectángulos y triángulos. Halla el área de cada pieza y luego suma. Si se recorta una pieza, réstala. Un cuarto en forma de L formado por un rectángulo de 9 × 6 y otro de 7 × 3 tiene un área de 54 + 21 = 75 pies cuadrados.

lessons.title: Determine the Volume of Rectangular Prisms
lessons.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges using length × width × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words volume, rectangular prism, cubic units, and edge.

vocabulary.definition: The number of unit cubes inside a rectangular prism. Formula: V = l × w × h.
vocabulary.termEs: Volumen con aristas de números enteros
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de cubos unitarios dentro de un prisma rectangular. Fórmula: V = l × w × h.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura sólida.

vocabulary.definition: A solid box shape with six flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura sólida en forma de caja con seis lados rectangulares.

vocabulary.definition: The units used to measure space inside, like cubic inches.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las unidades para medir el espacio interior, como pulgadas cúbicas.

vocabulary.definition: How long, how wide, and how tall a box is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan largo, ancho y alto es una caja.

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape that folds up into a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana que se dobla y forma un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: The line where two flat sides of a solid meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea donde se unen dos lados planos de un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: A cube that measures one unit on every edge.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un cubo que mide una unidad en cada arista.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My time capsule box is 6 long, 4 wide, and 3 tall. I write the formula: V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 6 × 4 × 3.
First I multiply two of them: 6 × 4 = 24.
Then I multiply by the last one: 24 × 3 = 72.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Volume with Whole Number Edges is multiplying only two of the three edges and stopping there — for example, seeing a box that is 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall, multiplying just 6 × 4 = 24, and calling that the volume, when 24 is only the area of the bottom face (in square inches), not the volume of the whole box. The height must also be multiplied in: V = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches. A second common mistake is adding the three edges instead of multiplying them (6 + 4 + 3 = 13 instead of 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic inches). Volume always MULTIPLIES all three edges, and the answer is always labeled in cubic units (in³), never square units (in²) or plain units (in).
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Volume is how many unit cubes fill a box. Multiply length × width × height. A box 5 cubes long, 3 wide, and 2 tall holds 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubes.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El volumen es cuántos cubos unitarios llenan una caja. Multiplica largo × ancho × alto. Una caja de 5 cubos de largo, 3 de ancho y 2 de alto contiene 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubos.

lessons.title: Represent Three-Dimensional Figures in Two Dimensions
lessons.objective: I can find the surface area of a solid by using its net.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words surface area, net, face, and two-dimensional.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of all the faces of a solid. A net unfolds the solid flat so you can see every face and add their areas.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de todas las caras de un cuerpo. Una plantilla lo despliega para ver cada cara y sumar sus áreas.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of all the flat sides of a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de todos los lados planos de un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape that folds up into a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana que se dobla y forma un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: One flat side of a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado plano de una figura sólida.

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape with length and width, but no thickness.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana con largo y ancho, pero sin grosor.

vocabulary.definition: The line where two flat sides of a solid meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea donde se unen dos lados planos de un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: A solid with one base and triangular sides that meet at a point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un sólido con una base y lados triangulares que se unen en un punto.

vocabulary.definition: A corner point where edges meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina donde se unen las aristas.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My box is 8 in. long, 5 in. wide, and 3 in. tall. I unfold it into a net and see 3 pairs of faces.
Top and bottom: each is 8 × 5 = 40, and there are 2 of them, so 2 × 40 = 80.
Front and back: each is 8 × 3 = 24, so 2 × 24 = 48.
Left and right: each is 5 × 3 = 15, so 2 × 15 = 30.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area Using Nets is finding the area of only one face from each of the 3 matching pairs and forgetting to double it, instead of counting all 6 faces. For a box that is 9 in × 4 in × 5 in, a student might add just one face from each pair: (9×4) + (9×5) + (4×5) = 36 + 45 + 20 = 101 in², but the net actually has two of each face, so the correct total is 2(36) + 2(45) + 2(20) = 72 + 90 + 40 = 202 in² — exactly double. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I count both matching faces in each pair, or only one from each pair?'
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Surface area is the total area of all the flat faces on the outside of a box — like the wrapping paper that covers it. Unfold the box flat (a net), find the area of each face, and add them up. A cube with 2-inch edges has 6 faces of 4 square inches each, so 6 × 4 = 24 square inches.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El área de superficie es el área total de todas las caras planas por fuera de una caja, como el papel de regalo que la cubre. Desdobla la caja en plano (una red), halla el área de cada cara y suma todas. Un cubo con aristas de 2 pulgadas tiene 6 caras de 4 pulgadas cuadradas cada una, así que 6 × 4 = 24 pulgadas cuadradas.

lessons.title: Determine Surface Area of Prisms
lessons.objective: I can find the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words surface area, rectangular prism, triangular prism, and face.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of all bases and lateral faces of a prism. Formula: SA = 2B + lateral area.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de las bases y caras laterales de un prisma. Fórmula: SA = 2B + área lateral.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of all the flat sides of a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de todos los lados planos de un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: A solid box shape with six flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura sólida en forma de caja con seis lados rectangulares.

vocabulary.definition: A solid with two triangle ends and three flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un sólido con dos extremos triangulares y tres lados rectangulares.

vocabulary.definition: One flat side of a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado plano de una figura sólida.

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape that folds up into a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana que se dobla y forma un sólido.

vocabulary.definition: The side faces of a solid, not the top or bottom.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los lados de un sólido, no la parte de arriba ni la de abajo.

vocabulary.definition: Exactly the same size and shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Exactamente del mismo tamaño y forma.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My triangular prism has triangle bases (base 6 in., height 4 in.), is 10 in. long, and the two slant sides are 5 in. each.
Each triangle base is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, and there are 2 of them: 2 × 12 = 24.
Now the 3 rectangles: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 10 = 50, and 5 × 10 = 50, which add to 160.
I add the bases and the rectangles: 24 + 160 = 184.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Prisms is confusing surface area with volume — multiplying l × w × h (which finds the space INSIDE the prism, in cubic units) instead of adding the areas of all the faces (SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh, in square units). A second common slip is forgetting to double one face pair, like writing 2(l×w) + 2(l×h) + (w×h) instead of + 2(w×h) — always count all 6 faces (or all 5 for a triangular prism) before you submit.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Surface area is the total area of every face on the outside of a solid: a box has 6 rectangles, and a triangular prism has 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangle sides. Add the areas of all the faces. A box 3 in by 2 in by 1 in has faces of 6, 6, 3, 3, 2, and 2 square inches, so its surface area is 22 square inches.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El área de superficie es el área total de todas las caras por fuera de un sólido: una caja tiene 6 rectángulos, y un prisma triangular tiene 2 triángulos en los extremos y 3 rectángulos a los lados. Suma las áreas de todas las caras. Una caja de 3 pulg por 2 pulg por 1 pulg tiene caras de 6, 6, 3, 3, 2 y 2 pulgadas cuadradas, así que su área de superficie es 22 pulgadas cuadradas.

lessons.title: Determine Surface Area of Pyramids
lessons.objective: I can find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the base area and the lateral faces.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words pyramid, slant height, lateral face, and base.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of a pyramid's base and triangular faces. Formula: SA = B + lateral area.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de la base y las caras triangulares de una pirámide. Fórmula: SA = B + área lateral.

vocabulary.definition: A solid with a flat bottom and triangle sides that meet at one point on top.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un sólido con un fondo plano y lados triangulares que se unen en un punto arriba.

vocabulary.definition: The height of a side triangle, measured along its slanted face.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La altura de un triángulo lateral, medida por su cara inclinada.

vocabulary.definition: A triangle side of a pyramid, not the bottom.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado triangular de una pirámide, no el fondo.

vocabulary.definition: The flat bottom of a pyramid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El fondo plano de una pirámide.

vocabulary.definition: The point at the top of a pyramid where the sides meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El punto en la parte de arriba de una pirámide donde se unen los lados.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of just the side triangles, not the bottom.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total solo de los triángulos laterales, sin el fondo.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of every face of a solid, base included.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de todas las caras de un sólido, incluida la base.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My square pyramid has a 6 in. × 6 in. base and a slant height of 8 in.
First the base area: 6 × 6 = 36.
Now one triangular face: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. A square pyramid has 4 of them, so 4 × 24 = 96.
I add the base and the side faces: 36 + 96 = 132.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Pyramids is finding the four triangular lateral faces correctly (½ × base edge × slant height, times 4) and then stopping — forgetting to add the base area at the end. This leaves the total surface area too small by exactly the base's area. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I add the base area to the four lateral faces, or did I stop after the sides?'
instructional.familyKeyIdea: The surface area of a pyramid is the area of its bottom plus the areas of its triangle sides. A square pyramid with a 6 in base edge and 5 in slant height: 6 × 6 = 36, each triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15, so 36 + 4 × 15 = 96 square inches.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El área de superficie de una pirámide es el área de su base más las áreas de sus caras triangulares. Una pirámide cuadrada con arista de la base de 6 pulg y altura inclinada de 5 pulg: 6 × 6 = 36, cada triángulo es ½ × 6 × 5 = 15, así que 36 + 4 × 15 = 96 pulgadas cuadradas.

lessons.title: Area of Regular Polygons
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into triangles.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words regular polygon, decompose, triangle, and composite.

vocabulary.definition: The space a regular polygon covers. Split it from the center into identical triangles, find one triangle's area, then multiply by how many there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio que cubre un polígono regular. Divídelo desde el centro en triángulos idénticos, halla el área de uno y multiplícala por cuántos hay.

vocabulary.definition: A closed flat shape made of straight sides, where every side is the same length and every angle is the same size.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana cerrada de lados rectos, donde todos los lados miden lo mismo y todos los ángulos son iguales.

vocabulary.definition: To break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar una figura en figuras más pequeñas y simples.

vocabulary.definition: A shape with three sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de tres lados.

vocabulary.definition: Made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet. Use the rounded height to estimate the area.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A regular polygon has equal sides. Split it from the middle into matching triangles. Find the area of one triangle, then multiply by how many triangles there are. A hexagon made of 6 triangles of 12 square cm each has area 6 × 12 = 72 square cm.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un polígono regular tiene lados iguales. Divídelo desde el centro en triángulos iguales. Halla el área de un triángulo y multiplícala por el número de triángulos. Un hexágono formado por 6 triángulos de 12 centímetros cuadrados cada uno tiene un área de 6 × 12 = 72 centímetros cuadrados.

lessons.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
lessons.objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism, including ones with fractional edge lengths, using base area × height.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words volume, rectangular prism, dimensions, and base area.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a rectangular prism. Formula: V = Bh = l × w × h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un prisma rectangular. Fórmula: V = Bh = l × w × h.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura sólida.

vocabulary.definition: A solid box shape with six flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura sólida en forma de caja con seis lados rectangulares.

vocabulary.definition: The units used to measure space inside, like cubic inches.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las unidades para medir el espacio interior, como pulgadas cúbicas.

vocabulary.definition: How long, how wide, and how tall a shape is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan largo, ancho y alto es una figura.

vocabulary.definition: The area of the bottom of a solid. Volume = base area × height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área del fondo de un sólido. Volumen = área de la base × altura.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: My capsule is 2 ft long, 1.5 ft wide, and 1 ft tall. I write V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1.
First I multiply 2 × 1.5 = 3.
Then 3 × 1 = 3.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Volume of Rectangular Prisms is rounding a fractional edge length to the nearest whole number before multiplying, instead of using the exact fraction or decimal. For a box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, a student might round 1.5 down to 1 and compute 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³, but the correct volume uses the exact edge length: 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — a full cubic foot larger. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I multiply using the exact fractional or decimal edge length, or did I round it off first?'
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Volume is the space inside a box. Multiply length × width × height, even when an edge is a fraction. A box 2 ft long, 1½ ft wide, and 1 ft tall holds 2 × 1½ × 1 = 3 cubic feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: El volumen es el espacio dentro de una caja. Multiplica largo × ancho × alto, aunque una arista sea una fracción. Una caja de 2 pies de largo, 1½ pies de ancho y 1 pie de alto contiene 2 × 1½ × 1 = 3 pies cúbicos.

lessons.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Whole Numbers
lessons.objective: I can explain what dividing with a whole number and a unit fraction means — how many groups fit, or how much is in one group — find the quotient with a model, and check it by multiplying.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain why dividing by a unit fraction gives the same answer as multiplying by its reciprocal, using the words reciprocal, divisor, and quotient.

vocabulary.definition: Finding how many groups of one fraction fit inside another amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar cuántos grupos de una fracción caben dentro de otra cantidad.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction turned upside down.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción volteada de arriba abajo.

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.

vocabulary.definition: The total number being divided into equal groups (the number inside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número total que se divide en partes iguales (el número dentro de la casilla de división).

vocabulary.definition: The number of equal groups you are dividing into (the number outside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número de partes iguales en las que divides (el número fuera de la casilla de división).

vocabulary.definition: A fraction with 1 on top, like 1/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción con 1 arriba, como 1/4.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers whose product is 1; each is the reciprocal of the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números cuyo producto es 1; cada uno es el recíproco del otro.

vocabulary.definition: A bar model cut into equal parts to show sharing or grouping.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un modelo de barra cortado en partes iguales para mostrar reparto o agrupación.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I want to cut a 3-foot strip of tape into 1/4-foot pieces, so I write 3 ÷ 1/4. It asks: how many 1/4-foot pieces fit in 3 feet?
Each foot holds 4 quarter-foot pieces, so 3 feet hold 3 × 4 = 12 pieces.
That is why the shortcut works: dividing by 1/4 gives the same answer as multiplying by its reciprocal, 4/1. So 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3/1 × 4/1 = 12. (Some people call this Keep, Change, Flip.)
Check by multiplying: 12 pieces × 1/4 foot = 12/4 = 3 feet. So 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12 pieces.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's do one together — the same problem the bar model showed
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Interpret Division of Fractions is assuming that dividing always makes the answer smaller. For 4 ÷ 1/3, students reason 'dividing shrinks the number' and compute 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.3 instead of asking how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 4 feet (each whole foot holds 3 thirds, so 4 × 3 = 12). Before you submit, check: if the divisor is a fraction smaller than 1, the quotient must be BIGGER than the dividend, not smaller.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Dividing by a fraction asks how many of those pieces fit. 3 ÷ 1/4 means: how many quarter-foot pieces fit in 3 feet? Each foot has 4 quarters, so 3 × 4 = 12. Check: 12 quarters make 3 feet.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Dividir entre una fracción pregunta cuántas de esas piezas caben. 3 ÷ 1/4 significa: ¿cuántas piezas de un cuarto de pie caben en 3 pies? Cada pie tiene 4 cuartos, así que 3 × 4 = 12. Comprueba: 12 cuartos forman 3 pies.

lessons.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
lessons.objective: I can explain what dividing a fraction by a fraction means, find the quotient with common denominators or by multiplying by the reciprocal, and check it by multiplying.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain why multiplying by the reciprocal works, using the words reciprocal, improper fraction, mixed number, and simplify.

vocabulary.definition: Multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar la primera fracción por el recíproco de la segunda fracción.

vocabulary.definition: The total number being divided into equal groups (the number inside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número total que se divide en partes iguales (el número dentro de la casilla de división).

vocabulary.definition: The number of equal groups you are dividing into (the number outside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número de partes iguales en las que divides (el número fuera de la casilla de división).

vocabulary.definition: A fraction turned upside down.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción volteada de arriba abajo.

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.

vocabulary.definition: To write a fraction with smaller numbers that names the same amount, like 2/4 = 1/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una fracción con números más pequeños que nombra la misma cantidad, como 2/4 = 1/2.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number and a fraction written together, like 2 1/2. It must be rewritten as an improper fraction before dividing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero y una fracción escritos juntos, como 2 1/2. Debe reescribirse como fracción impropia antes de dividir.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator, like 5/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción cuyo numerador es mayor o igual que su denominador, como 5/2.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Agent Rivera has 3/4 pound and each portion is 1/8 pound. I want 3/4 ÷ 1/8.
It asks how many 1/8-pound portions fit in 3/4 pound. I rename 3/4 in eighths: 3/4 = 6/8.
6 eighths ÷ 1 eighth = 6, the same way 6 apples ÷ 1 apple = 6. That is the common-denominator method.
The reciprocal shortcut gives the same answer: 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6, because each pound holds 8 eighths. Check: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4. She can make 6 portions.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Dividing fractions asks how many of one piece fit in another. 3/4 ÷ 1/8: write 3/4 as 6/8, and 6 eighths hold 6 pieces of 1/8. So the answer is 6. Check: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Dividir fracciones pregunta cuántas piezas de un tamaño caben en otra cantidad. 3/4 ÷ 1/8: escribe 3/4 como 6/8, y 6 octavos tienen 6 piezas de 1/8. Así que la respuesta es 6. Comprueba: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4.

lessons.title: Explore Numerical Expressions with Exponents
lessons.objective: I can write and evaluate numbers in exponent form using a base and a power.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words exponent, base, power, and evaluate.

vocabulary.definition: A power uses a base and an exponent to show repeated multiplication.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una potencia usa una base y un exponente para mostrar multiplicación repetida.

vocabulary.definition: A small number that tells how many times to multiply a number by itself.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número pequeño que dice cuántas veces multiplicar un número por sí mismo.

vocabulary.definition: The number that gets multiplied by itself.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que se multiplica por sí mismo.

vocabulary.definition: A number written with a base and an exponent, like 2³.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número escrito con una base y un exponente, como 2³.

vocabulary.definition: To find the value by putting numbers in for the letters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Encontrar el valor poniendo números en lugar de las letras.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying the same factor again and again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar el mismo factor una y otra vez.

vocabulary.definition: A power written out as a product of its factors.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una potencia escrita como el producto de sus factores.

vocabulary.definition: A base used as a factor two times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una base usada como factor dos veces.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I want to find the value of 2³.
The small 3 tells me to multiply 2 by itself 3 times.
So I write 2 × 2 × 2.
First 2 × 2 = 4. Then 4 × 2 = 8.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Powers and Exponents is multiplying the base by the exponent instead of using the base as a repeated factor — for example, thinking 2³ = 2 × 3 = 6 instead of 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. Before you submit, rewrite the power as repeated multiplication first, then multiply step by step.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: An exponent tells how many times to multiply a number by itself. For example, 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un exponente dice cuántas veces se multiplica un número por sí mismo. Por ejemplo, 2³ significa 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, no 2 × 3 = 6.

lessons.title: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
lessons.objective: I can write numerical expressions from a real situation and evaluate them using the order of operations, including powers.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words expression, evaluate, order of operations, base, and exponent.

vocabulary.term: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
vocabulary.definition: Turning a situation into a number sentence without an equal sign, then finding its value in the correct order.
vocabulary.termEs: Escribir y evaluar expresiones numéricas con exponentes
vocabulary.definitionEs: Convertir una situación en una expresión numérica sin signo de igual y luego hallar su valor en el orden correcto.

vocabulary.definition: A math phrase built from numbers and operations, with no equal sign and no variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una frase matemática hecha de números y operaciones, sin signo de igual y sin variable.

vocabulary.definition: To find the single value an expression is worth by carrying out its operations in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar el único valor que representa una expresión, realizando sus operaciones en orden.

vocabulary.definition: The agreed order for evaluating: grouping symbols, then exponents, then multiply and divide left to right, then add and subtract left to right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El orden acordado para evaluar: signos de agrupación, luego exponentes, luego multiplicar y dividir de izquierda a derecha, y por último sumar y restar de izquierda a derecha.

vocabulary.definition: A short way to write repeated multiplication of the same factor, such as 2³ for 2 × 2 × 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma corta de escribir la multiplicación repetida del mismo factor, como 2³ para 2 × 2 × 2.

vocabulary.definition: In a power, the number being multiplied by itself. In 2³ the base is 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: En una potencia, el número que se multiplica por sí mismo. En 2³ la base es 2.

vocabulary.definition: In a power, the small raised number that says how many times the base is used as a factor.
vocabulary.definitionEs: En una potencia, el número pequeño elevado que indica cuántas veces se usa la base como factor.

vocabulary.definition: Parentheses or brackets; the work inside them is done first.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Paréntesis o corchetes; el trabajo dentro de ellos se hace primero.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Sofia buys 2 member tickets at $15, 4 non-member tickets at $20, and 8 student tickets at $2 each. I write one expression for each ticket type: 2 × 15, 4 × 20, and 8 × 2.
The whole order is the three costs added together: 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2.
Now I evaluate. There are no grouping symbols and no powers yet, so multiplication comes first, left to right: 30 + 80 + 16.
Then I add: 30 + 80 + 16 = 126. The tickets cost $126.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake with powers is multiplying the base by the exponent: reading 3² as 3 × 2 = 6 instead of 3 × 3 = 9. A second is evaluating strictly left to right, so 3 + 4 × 2 becomes 14 instead of 11. The order of operations exists so one expression has exactly one value: grouping symbols, then powers, then × and ÷ left to right, then + and − left to right.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: To find the value of a math expression, follow the order: parentheses first, then exponents, then multiply or divide, then add or subtract. In 2 × 15 + 8 × 2³, first 2³ = 8, then 30 + 64 = 94.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Para hallar el valor de una expresión matemática, sigue el orden: primero los paréntesis, luego los exponentes, luego multiplicar o dividir, y por último sumar o restar. En 2 × 15 + 8 × 2³, primero 2³ = 8, luego 30 + 64 = 94.

lessons.title: Write and Evaluate Algebraic Expressions
lessons.objective: I can write an algebraic expression for a real situation and evaluate it for a given value of the variable.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my expression using the words variable, term, coefficient, constant, substitute, and evaluate.

vocabulary.definition: Translate words or a situation into numbers, variables, and operation symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Traducir palabras o una situación a números, variables y símbolos de operaciones.

vocabulary.definition: A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.

vocabulary.definition: A math phrase that has at least one letter.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una frase matemática que tiene al menos una letra.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número frente a una letra, como el 3 en 3x.

vocabulary.definition: A fixed number in an expression or equation that does not change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número fijo en una expresión o ecuación que no cambia.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.

vocabulary.definition: To replace a variable with a given number before working out the value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reemplazar una variable por un número dado antes de calcular el valor.

vocabulary.definition: To find what an expression is worth once every variable has a number, following the order of operations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar cuánto vale una expresión una vez que cada variable tiene un número, siguiendo el orden de las operaciones.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Tickets cost $12 each, plus a flat $50 venue fee. Let t be the number of tickets.
"$12 each ticket" means 12 times t, which I write as 12t.
The flat fee $50 is added once, so I add 50.
I put them together: total revenue = 12t + 50.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Algebraic Expressions is treating 'each' or 'per' as if it means add instead of multiply, and attaching the variable to the wrong number. For 'a $25 setup fee plus $8 per hour, h,' students often write 25 + 8 + h (adding all three numbers) or 25h + 8 (multiplying the flat fee by h) instead of the correct 8h + 25. Since $8 applies per hour, it must multiply the variable (8h), and the flat $25 fee is a constant added only once — check that the per-unit rate, not the flat fee, is the number multiplied by the variable.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A letter like s can stand for a number that changes, such as how many students there are. If shirts cost $4 each and shipping is $20 once, the cost is 4s + 20. For 10 students: 4 × 10 + 20 = $60.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Una letra como s puede representar un número que cambia, como la cantidad de estudiantes. Si cada camiseta cuesta $4 y el envío cuesta $20 una sola vez, el costo es 4s + 20. Para 10 estudiantes: 4 × 10 + 20 = $60.

lessons.title: Identify Equivalent Algebraic Expressions
lessons.objective: I can show that two expressions are equivalent by simplifying and combining like terms.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words equivalent, simplify, like terms, and combine.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that look different but have the same value for every allowed variable value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que se ven diferentes pero tienen el mismo valor para cada valor permitido de la variable.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that always have the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que siempre tienen el mismo valor.

vocabulary.definition: To rewrite an expression in a shorter form that is still equal to the original.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una expresión en una forma más corta que sigue siendo igual a la original.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar o restar términos con la misma letra en uno solo.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número frente a una letra, como el 3 en 3x.

vocabulary.definition: The order of the numbers can change in addition or multiplication without changing the result.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El orden de los números puede cambiar en una suma o una multiplicación sin cambiar el resultado.

vocabulary.definition: The grouping of the numbers can change in addition or multiplication without changing the result.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La agrupación de los números puede cambiar en una suma o una multiplicación sin cambiar el resultado.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Producer A wrote 3x + 2x + 10 and Producer B wrote 5x + 10. Are they equivalent?
Both give 30, and 3x + 2x is just 5x, so they are equivalent.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equivalent Expressions is adding the exponents instead of the coefficients when combining like terms — writing 3x + 2x as 5x² instead of 5x. Remember: 3x means 3 groups of x and 2x means 2 more groups of x, so you add the coefficients (3 + 2 = 5) and keep the variable's power the same (x¹, not x²).
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Two expressions are equivalent when they always give the same answer. 3x + 2x + 10 and 5x + 10 are equivalent: try x = 2 and both equal 20.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Dos expresiones son equivalentes cuando siempre dan la misma respuesta. 3x + 2x + 10 y 5x + 10 son equivalentes: prueba con x = 2 y las dos dan 20.

lessons.title: Find Factors and Multiples
lessons.objective: I can find the greatest common factor and the least common multiple of two numbers, and use each to solve a real problem.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my choice using the words factor, multiple, common, greatest, and least.

vocabulary.definition: Listing what divides a number evenly (its factors) and what it divides into evenly (its multiples), then finding what two numbers share.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Listar lo que divide un número exactamente (sus factores) y lo que el número forma al contar de esa cantidad (sus múltiplos), y luego hallar lo que dos números comparten.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number that divides another number evenly, with no remainder.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero que divide a otro exactamente, sin residuo.

vocabulary.definition: The result of multiplying a number by 1, 2, 3, and so on — where you land when you skip-count by it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El resultado de multiplicar un número por 1, 2, 3, y así sucesivamente: donde caes al contar de esa cantidad.

vocabulary.definition: The largest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. It answers “how many equal groups can I make?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más grande que es factor de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuántos grupos iguales puedo formar?”

vocabulary.definition: The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. It answers “when will these line up again?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número más pequeño que es múltiplo de dos o más números. Responde “¿cuándo volverán a coincidir?”

vocabulary.definition: Two factors that multiply to make a number. In a word problem, one is the number of groups and the other is the size of each group.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos factores que se multiplican para formar un número. En un problema, uno es la cantidad de grupos y el otro el tamaño de cada grupo.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers, usually with a factor tree. Multiplying the primes two numbers share also gives the GCF.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como producto de números primos, normalmente con un árbol de factores. Multiplicar los primos que dos números comparten también da el MCD.

vocabulary.definition: A factor that two numbers both have.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor que dos números tienen en común.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The store has 48 pencils and 36 notebooks. Every combo pack must hold the same number of each, with nothing left over — so the number of packs has to be a factor of BOTH quantities.
Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Listing them in order is what makes the comparison easy.
The numbers in both lists are the common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.
The greatest of those is 12, so the GCF of 48 and 36 is 12. The manager can make 12 combo packs — each holding 48 ÷ 12 = 4 pencils and 36 ÷ 12 = 3 notebooks.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's do one together — the same GCF, using prime factors
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake is reaching for the wrong tool: listing FACTORS for a problem about repeating cycles. Ayasha's classes repeat every 6 and 8 weeks, so the weeks they land on are multiples — answering with the GCF of 2 claims a class that meets every 8 weeks happens in week 2. Use the size of the answer as a check: a GCF is never larger than the smaller number, and an LCM is never smaller than the larger one.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: A factor divides a number evenly: 4 is a factor of 12. A multiple is what you get when you skip-count: 12, 24, 36 are multiples of 12. Use the greatest common factor to split things into equal groups, and the least common multiple to find when two repeating events happen together.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Un factor divide a un número exactamente: 4 es factor de 12. Un múltiplo es lo que obtienes al contar de salto en salto: 12, 24, 36 son múltiplos de 12. Usa el máximo común divisor para repartir en grupos iguales, y el mínimo común múltiplo para saber cuándo dos sucesos que se repiten coinciden.

lessons.title: Generate Equivalent Expressions
lessons.objective: I can use the commutative, associative, and identity properties to rewrite expressions.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words commutative property, associative property, and identity property.

vocabulary.definition: Rules that let you reorder or regroup numbers without changing an expression's value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reglas que permiten reordenar o reagrupar números sin cambiar el valor de una expresión.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the order and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar el orden y obtener la misma respuesta.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the grouping and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar la agrupación y obtener la misma respuesta.

vocabulary.definition: Adding 0 or multiplying by 1 keeps the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar 0 o multiplicar por 1 mantiene el mismo valor.

vocabulary.definition: A rule that is always true in math.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla que siempre es verdadera en matemáticas.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying a number by everything inside the parentheses: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar un número por todo lo que está dentro del paréntesis: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that have the same value for every value of the variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que tienen el mismo valor para todo valor de la variable.

vocabulary.definition: Multiply out an expression to remove the parentheses.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar una expresión para eliminar los paréntesis.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I have 3 guitarists, 5 drummers, and 2 keyboard players.
I can add them as 3 + 5 + 2, which gives 10.
The Commutative Property says order does not matter: 5 + 3 + 2 also gives 10.
The Associative Property says grouping does not matter: (3 + 5) + 2 = 3 + (5 + 2), both equal 10.
instructional.commonMistake: A common mistake in Properties of Operations is applying the commutative property where it does not belong, or confusing it with the associative property. Students often assume 15 − 8 = 8 − 15 (it does not: 7 ≠ −7 — commutative only works for addition and multiplication), or they see parentheses move and call it "associative" even when the numbers inside just swapped places, like (2 + 3) + 4 = (3 + 2) + 4 (that is commutative — the order inside the parentheses changed, not the grouping). Before you label a property, ask: did only the order change (commutative), did only the grouping change (associative), or was a 0 or 1 involved (identity)?
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Some math rules let you change how numbers are written without changing the answer. You can add or multiply in any order, like 3 + 5 = 5 + 3, or group numbers in a new way, like (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4). You can also share a multiplier with each part: 3(2 + 4) = 3 × 2 + 3 × 4 = 18.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Algunas reglas de matemáticas te permiten cambiar cómo se escriben los números sin cambiar la respuesta. Puedes sumar o multiplicar en cualquier orden, como 3 + 5 = 5 + 3, o agrupar los números de otra manera, como (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4). También puedes repartir un multiplicador entre cada parte: 3(2 + 4) = 3 × 2 + 3 × 4 = 18.
