lessons.title: Apply Two-Variable Relationships to Solve Problems
lessons.objective: I can write an equation to represent the relationship between two variable quantities and use it to solve a real problem.
lessons.languageObjective: I can justify a recommendation using the words equation, solution, and at least.

vocabulary.definition: A value of the variable that makes an equation true.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un valor de la variable que hace que una ecuación sea verdadera.

vocabulary.definition: To replace a variable with a number so you can compute.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reemplazar una variable con un número para poder calcular.

vocabulary.definition: That amount or more — the smallest amount that still works.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Esa cantidad o más — la cantidad mínima que todavía funciona.

vocabulary.definition: To make a reasonable guess about a future amount using information you already have.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hacer una estimación razonable sobre una cantidad futura usando la información que ya tienes.

vocabulary.definition: To explain WHY an answer or recommendation makes sense, using the mathematics.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Explicar POR QUÉ una respuesta o recomendación tiene sentido, usando las matemáticas.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equals sign showing two amounts are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un enunciado matemático con un signo igual que muestra que dos cantidades son iguales.

vocabulary.definition: The operation that undoes another one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La operación que deshace otra.

vocabulary.definition: Start from the output and undo each step to find the input.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Empezar desde el resultado y deshacer cada paso para encontrar la entrada.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: The number of cars produced depends on the number of hours of operation. Every hour, the plant produces 2.5 cars.
Let h = hours and c = cars. The equation is c = 2.5h. Check with the table: 8 hours gives 2.5 × 8 = 20 cars per shift.
The order needs 1,000 cars, so substitute: 2.5h = 1,000.
Divide both sides by 2.5: h = 1,000 ÷ 2.5 = 400 hours.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's plan the car wash together
instructional.commonMistake: Adding the rate instead of multiplying — writing 2.5 + 8 = 10.5 cars for an 8-hour shift instead of 2.5 × 8 = 20. The rate applies to EVERY hour, so the total is always rate × amount.
instructional.familyKeyIdea: Use an equation to answer real questions: put in the number you know, solve for the one you don't, and check that the answer makes sense. If a car goes 50 miles each hour, d = 50h. To go 200 miles, 50h = 200, so h = 4 hours.
instructional.familyKeyIdeaEs: Usa una ecuación para contestar preguntas reales: pon el número que sabes, resuelve para el que no sabes y comprueba que la respuesta tenga sentido. Si un carro recorre 50 millas cada hora, d = 50h. Para recorrer 200 millas, 50h = 200, así que h = 4 horas.

lessons.title: Math is Everywhere
lessons.objective: I can find applications of math outside of school — in professions like being a chef, in hobbies like gardening, and around my own house.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe how someone uses math at work using the words plan, calculate, and measure.

vocabulary.definition: A job someone is trained to do, like chef, nurse, or carpenter.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un trabajo para el que alguien se ha preparado, como chef, enfermero o carpintero.

vocabulary.definition: The supply of items a business keeps on hand, tracked by counting.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las existencias que un negocio tiene disponibles, controladas contándolas.

vocabulary.definition: The measured amount of food served to one person.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad medida de comida que se sirve a una persona.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of flat space a surface covers, measured in square units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio plano que cubre una superficie, medida en unidades cuadradas.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of space something fills, measured in cubic units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio que algo ocupa, medida en unidades cúbicas.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: When chefs plan menus, they determine the number of items on the menu and calculate the price point for each item.
They decide on the portion size of each item and project how much food is needed for each day.
They calculate how much of each ingredient to order — that is counting, measuring, and multiplying, all before a single dish is cooked.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's find the math in a garden together
instructional.commonMistake: Believing math only 'counts' when it happens in a classroom — and walking past the calculating, measuring, and projecting inside jobs, hobbies, and chores every day.

lessons.title: Math is Beauty
lessons.objective: I can use bilateral symmetry to describe structure in nature and in human creations.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe a symmetric design using the words mirror image, line of symmetry, and balance.

vocabulary.definition: Having two halves that match — one side is a mirror image of the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Que tiene dos mitades que coinciden: un lado es la imagen reflejada del otro.

vocabulary.definition: A copy of a figure flipped across a line, so the two halves face each other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una copia de una figura volteada al otro lado de una línea, de modo que las dos mitades se miran entre sí.

vocabulary.definition: Reflective symmetry in plants and animals — the two sides of the body mirror each other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La simetría reflectiva en plantas y animales: los dos lados del cuerpo se reflejan entre sí.

vocabulary.definition: The line you can draw through a figure so each side is a reflection of the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea que puedes trazar por una figura de modo que cada lado sea el reflejo del otro.

vocabulary.definition: An even, steady arrangement — neither side feels heavier than the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una disposición pareja y estable: ningún lado se siente más pesado que el otro.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: I look at the two sides of the butterfly, and they look like mirror images — the butterfly is symmetric.
All butterflies have reflective symmetry. In plants and animals, this is called bilateral symmetry.
To show it, I draw a line down the middle of the butterfly's body: everything on the left is reflected on the right.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's find the symmetry in a growing plant
instructional.commonMistake: Thinking a figure lacks bilateral symmetry just because its line of symmetry is not vertical — the mirror line can run in any direction, and the test is whether the two sides match across it.

lessons.title: Math is Playful
lessons.objective: I can use patterns and relationships to make sense of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and think logically about its solutions.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe a puzzle strategy using the words pattern, rule, and predict.

vocabulary.definition: A problem designed to be played with — it has rules, a goal, and room to imagine solutions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un problema diseñado para jugarse: tiene reglas, una meta y espacio para imaginar soluciones.

vocabulary.definition: Something that repeats or changes in a predictable way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que se repite o cambia de una manera predecible.

vocabulary.definition: A rule that tells you how to get the next value in a pattern from the one before it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla que te dice cómo obtener el siguiente valor de un patrón a partir del anterior.

vocabulary.definition: To say what will happen before it happens, using a pattern or reasoning.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Decir lo que va a pasar antes de que pase, usando un patrón o el razonamiento.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange information — often in a table — so patterns become easier to see.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ordenar la información, muchas veces en una tabla, para que los patrones sean más fáciles de ver.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: Before moving anything, I describe what the solved puzzle will look like: the discs in the same order — smallest on top to largest on bottom — but on a different rod.
Then I play the small cases: a one-disc tower takes 1 move, and a two-disc tower takes 3 moves.
A three-disc tower takes at least 7 moves. Small cases are how mathematicians play.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's organize the moves in a table
instructional.commonMistake: Doubling the previous number of steps but forgetting to add 1 — answering 14 instead of 15 for four discs, or 30 instead of 31 for five.

lessons.title: Math is Ingenuity
lessons.objective: I can use ratios and models to explain how the Penny Farthing and gear-driven bicycles were ingenious solutions to a real problem.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain a gear ratio using the words rotation, teeth, and 'for each ___, the wheel turns ___.'

vocabulary.definition: Coming up with different, and sometimes unique, solutions to problems.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Idear soluciones diferentes, y a veces únicas, a los problemas.

vocabulary.definition: One full turn of a wheel, gear, or pedal all the way around.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una vuelta completa de una rueda, un engranaje o un pedal.

vocabulary.definition: A toothed wheel that passes motion to another toothed wheel through a chain.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una rueda con dientes que transmite el movimiento a otra rueda con dientes por medio de una cadena.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of two quantities, like pedal rotations to wheel rotations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de dos cantidades, como rotaciones del pedal y rotaciones de la rueda.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that make the same comparison using different numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que hacen la misma comparación con números diferentes.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A later bicycle design uses a chain: the pedal gear has 48 teeth, and the largest rear gear has 32 teeth.
For each rotation of the 48-tooth pedal gear, the wheel gear also turns 48 teeth.
The 32-tooth gear needs to turn 32 teeth to make one full rotation, so I find the equivalent ratio: 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5.
The rear wheel makes 1.5 rotations for each pedal rotation — this gear makes it easier to pedal at slower speeds or go uphill.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's do the smallest gear together
instructional.commonMistake: Thinking a rear gear with MORE teeth makes the wheel spin more — it is the opposite: the 32-tooth gear gives only 1.5 rotations per pedal rotation, while the 12-tooth gear gives 4.

lessons.title: Math is Boundless
lessons.objective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next.
lessons.languageObjective: I can describe a design using the words repetition, pattern, pattern unit, and rhythm.

vocabulary.definition: The same object, shape, or form repeated multiple times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mismo objeto, figura o forma repetido varias veces.

vocabulary.definition: A set of objects or shapes that are repeated and arranged in a regular order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de objetos o figuras que se repiten y se organizan en un orden regular.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La parte más pequeña de un patrón que se repite.

vocabulary.definition: A design element created by varying the placement, size, orientation, or order of the same objects or shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un elemento de diseño creado al variar la posición, el tamaño, la orientación o el orden de los mismos objetos o figuras.

vocabulary.definition: Being able to know what comes next because the design follows a rule.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Poder saber qué viene después porque el diseño sigue una regla.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: A border repeats: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, ...
The pattern unit is 3 shapes long: circle, square, triangle.
To predict shape number 12, I divide: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.
The next three shapes after any complete unit will be a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.
instructional.commonMistake: Calling every repeated design a 'pattern.' One identical shape repeated is repetition; a pattern needs a unit of shapes repeating in a regular order; and rhythm varies the shapes' size and order, so it is neither.

lessons.title: Math is Mine
lessons.objective: I can look back at my answers from Lesson 1-1, describe how my math biography has changed this year, and recognize ways we are all doers of math.
lessons.languageObjective: I can compare my beginning-of-year and end-of-year math stories using the words then, now, changed, and grown.

vocabulary.definition: The story of your relationship with math — and how it has changed over time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La historia de tu relación con las matemáticas y cómo ha cambiado con el tiempo.

vocabulary.definition: To look back at what you did, felt, and learned, and think about what it means.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar atrás a lo que hiciste, sentiste y aprendiste, y pensar en lo que significa.

vocabulary.definition: The change between what you could do before and what you can do now.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El cambio entre lo que podías hacer antes y lo que puedes hacer ahora.

vocabulary.definition: Trusting yourself to try a problem, even when the first attempt might fail.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Confiar en ti mismo para intentar un problema, aunque el primer intento pueda fallar.

vocabulary.definition: The people and places around you — where math shows up outside the classroom.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las personas y los lugares que te rodean, donde las matemáticas aparecen fuera del aula.

sentenceFrames: The model shows ___ so the answer is ___.

workedExampleLines: In September I estimated the Ferris wheel: 20 cars with about 4 riders each is 20 × 4 = 80 riders — 'about 80.'
Now I can go further with this year's math: at 6 turns an hour, that wheel moves about 80 × 6 = 480 riders per hour.
Same wheel, same me — but my toolbox grew. That difference IS my math story.
instructional.weDoPrompt: Let's revisit 78.5 with this year's tools
instructional.commonMistake: Treating your math story as finished — writing the same answers you wrote in Lesson 1-1 instead of looking for what actually changed. The story grows and evolves; a retrospective that copies September has missed the point.
